name: Marcus Delaney, Burn ICU (22% TBSA, inhalation injury, burn sepsis)

caseMeta.title: Burn ICU: Thermal burn 22% TBSA with smoke inhalation, burn wound sepsis (3-day ICU stay to Med-Surg transfer)
learningObjectives: Calculate and implement burn fluid resuscitation with the Parkland formula (4 mL x kg x %TBSA), titrating lactated Ringer's hourly to a urine output goal of 0.5 mL/kg/h.
Recognize and respond to inhalation injury and carbon monoxide poisoning, and explain why a pulse oximeter reads falsely normal with carboxyhemoglobin.
Provide safe care for an intubated, sedated patient: ventilator bundle, RASS and CPOT, daily sedation interruption, spontaneous breathing trial and extubation readiness.
Perform and document hourly neurovascular and compartment checks after an escharotomy and recognize loss of perfusion.
Manage lines and tubes in a burn ICU: arterial line, central line, OG tube feeding, Foley, restraint safety, and infection prevention.
Recognize early burn wound infection and sepsis from vital sign trends and wound changes; communicate with SBAR; carry out the sepsis bundle and vasopressor titration.
Interpret trends in labs (lactate, WBC, platelets, creatinine, procalcitonin), cultures, ABG and I&O across a 3-day stay.
Plan nutrition, glucose control, pain and delirium prevention for a hypermetabolic burn patient.
Prepare a safe SBAR handoff for transfer from the ICU to a medical-surgical unit.

encounter.attending: R. Okafor, MD (Burn Surgery); L. Brandt, MD (Critical Care)
encounter.diagnosis: Thermal burns 22% TBSA (flame) with smoke inhalation injury and carbon monoxide poisoning; acute respiratory failure on mechanical ventilation
encounter.chiefComplaint: House fire victim with burns to the right arm, chest and face
encounter.ambulationOrder: Bed rest, HOB 30 degrees or higher

problems.name: Thermal burn, 22% TBSA (flame): full-thickness right forearm/hand, deep partial anterior chest and right upper arm, partial face/neck
problems.details: Injury 01:30 Mon 11-02. Circumferential right arm burn, escharotomy 03:15. About 8% TBSA full thickness. Parkland resuscitation 7,216 mL goal in 24 h from injury. OR for excision and grafting tentatively Fri 11-06.

problems.name: Smoke inhalation injury with carbon monoxide poisoning
problems.details: COHb 14.2% at 02:50. Bronchoscopy 04:20: grade 2 inhalation injury. Inhalation injury protocol: albuterol, nebulized heparin and acetylcysteine.

problems.name: Acute respiratory failure, intubated (ETT 02:50)
problems.details: AC/VC, VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW). Sedation with propofol and fentanyl; daily sedation interruption and spontaneous breathing trial.

problems.name: Hypermetabolic state, nutrition risk
problems.details: Early enteral feeding via OG tube; prealbumin low; electrolyte shifts.

problems.name: Alcohol use (4-6 beers on weekends); tobacco use 1 ppd
problems.details: Ethanol 42 mg/dL at 02:40. Thiamine and folate; monitor for withdrawal and delirium.

problems.name: Burn wound infection with sepsis (MSSA)
problems.details: Recognized Tue 11-03 about 15:30: purulent right arm/chest wound, fever, tachycardia, hypotension needing norepinephrine. MSSA in wound and 2 of 4 blood culture bottles. Cefazolin from Thu 06:10.

orders.name: etomidate (AMIDATE) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg IV Once.

orders.name: rocuronium (ZEMURON) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mg IV Once.

orders.name: fentanyl injection
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mcg IV Once x2.

orders.name: albuterol nebulizer solution
orders.instructions: Administer 2.5 mg Inhalation Once.

orders.name: tetanus, diphtheria and acellular pertussis vaccine (Tdap, ADACEL)
orders.instructions: Administer 0.5 mL Intramuscular Once.
orders.rationale: Tetanus prophylaxis for burn wounds (last booster unknown)

orders.name: lactated Ringer's (EMS bolus, prehospital)
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mL IV Once.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's 1,000 mL (burn resuscitation, Parkland)
orders.instructions: Lactated Ringer's, rate per protocol: start 450 mL/h (first 8 h from injury), then 225 mL/h (hours 8-24 from injury). TITRATE HOURLY to urine output 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h = 41 mL/h). If UOP under 30 mL/h for 2 consecutive hours increase rate 20-25%; if over 50 mL/h for 2 hours decrease rate 20-25%. Notify burn team for UOP under 20 mL/h or rate over 600 mL/h.
orders.rationale: Parkland formula 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% TBSA = 7,216 mL in 24 h from injury (01:30). Half in the first 8 h, half over the next 16 h.
nursingConsiderations: Record the rate change and the reason on the flowsheet every hour
Notify burn team if hourly urine output under 20 mL/h or over 100 mL/h
Check airway pressures, bladder pressure and right hand pulses with each rate increase

medication.importantInfo: Fluid creep: over-resuscitation causes pulmonary edema, compartment syndrome and ventilator days.

orders.name: sodium chloride 0.9% (carrier / KVO via central line)
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mL/h IV Continuous.
orders.rationale: Keep vein open after LR stopped

orders.name: propofol (DIPRIVAN) infusion 10 mg/mL
orders.instructions: Titrate by 5 mcg/kg/min every 5-10 minutes to RASS goal (-2 to -3 day 1; -1 to -2 day 2; 0 to -1 day 3). Daily sedation interruption at 08:00. Check triglycerides at 48 h. Change tubing every 12 h.

medication.importantInfo: Lipid emulsion: 1.1 kcal/mL, count calories. Use aseptic technique, hang time 12 h. Watch hypotension, especially with bolus or rate increase.

orders.name: fentanyl infusion 10 mcg/mL
orders.instructions: Titrate by 25 mcg/h every 15 minutes to CPOT under 3. Hold and notify for RR under 8 (non-ventilated) or SBP under 90. Stop at extubation.
orders.rationale: Analgesia for burn pain and ventilation

medication.importantInfo: Opioid-naive patient. Hold sedation interruption reassessment: pain still treated when sedation is lightened.

orders.name: norepinephrine (LEVOPHED) infusion 16 mcg/mL
orders.frequency: Continuous, titrate to MAP at least 65
orders.instructions: Central line only. Titrate by 0.02 mcg/kg/min every 5 minutes to MAP 65 or higher (max 0.5 mcg/kg/min without ICU attending approval). Wean by 0.02 mcg/kg/min every 15-30 min when MAP over 75. Check IV site and extremity perfusion each hour.
orders.rationale: Septic shock, MAP 64 after fluid boluses

medication.importantInfo: Extravasation causes tissue necrosis. Never infuse with other drugs in the same lumen. Verify concentration 4 mg/250 mL (16 mcg/mL). Dose based on 82 kg: 0.1 mcg/kg/min = 8.2 mcg/min = 30.8 mL/h.
medication.freqKey: Continuous, titrate to MAP at least 65

orders.name: insulin regular (HUMULIN R) infusion 1 unit/mL
orders.instructions: ICU insulin protocol: glucose every hour. Goal 140-180 mg/dL. Adjust rate per protocol table. Hold and call if glucose under 100 or tube feeding held. Notify for glucose under 70 (give D50 per protocol).
orders.rationale: Stress hyperglycemia, two consecutive glucose over 180

medication.importantInfo: Hypoglycemia risk increases when tube feeds are held or interrupted. Always recheck glucose 15 minutes after any change in feeds.

orders.name: dexmedetomidine (PRECEDEX) infusion 4 mcg/mL
orders.instructions: Hold for HR under 50 or SBP under 90 and notify the provider. Titrate 0.1 mcg/kg/h to RASS 0 to -1. Goal arousable and calm.
orders.rationale: Anxiety and agitation after extubation without respiratory depression

medication.importantInfo: Causes bradycardia and hypotension. Patient stays arousable (no respiratory depression).

orders.name: albumin human 5% injection 500 mL
orders.instructions: Infuse 500 mL over 4 hours (125 mL/h) via central line. Replace part of the LR. Monitor for fluid overload.
orders.rationale: Colloid resuscitation after 24 h from injury (albumin 2.6 at 06:00), reduces crystalloid volume

medication.importantInfo: Count as IV intake. Watch for pulmonary edema, elevated CVP, and new crackles.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's 500 mL bolus
orders.instructions: Give 500 mL over 30 minutes, reassess MAP, lung sounds, SpO2 and urine output, then repeat once if MAP below 65.

orders.name: piperacillin-tazobactam (ZOSYN) 4.5 g in 100 mL, extended infusion
orders.instructions: Extended infusion over 4 hours. Give through its own lumen when possible (separate lumens from vancomycin; the combination is associated with kidney injury). NO known drug allergies.
orders.rationale: Burn wound sepsis, broad coverage until cultures result

medication.importantInfo: Dosed with creatinine in mind. Stop when MSSA identified and cefazolin started (stewardship).

orders.name: vancomycin (VANCOCIN) IV
orders.instructions: Infuse over 2 hours (max 1 g/h). Monitor for red man syndrome (slow the rate). Pharmacy follows levels and creatinine. Stop when MSSA identified.
orders.rationale: MRSA coverage until cultures finalize; pharmacy dosing (about 20 mg/kg, rounded to 1,750 mg)

medication.importantInfo: Nephrotoxic. Creatinine 1.4 on Wed 05:00; level 11.6 before the second dose.

orders.name: cefazolin (ANCEF) 2 g in 100 mL
orders.instructions: Infuse over 30 minutes. Duration will be set by ID (blood cultures repeat negative at 24 h).
orders.rationale: MSSA bacteremia and burn wound infection (targeted therapy, replaces pip-tazo and vancomycin)

orders.name: hydrocortisone sodium succinate (SOLU-CORTEF) injection
orders.frequency: Every 6 hours, then 25 mg q6h from 14:30 Wed
orders.instructions: 50 mg q6h x3 doses, then 25 mg q6h until stopped by ICU team. Monitor glucose.

medication.freqKey: Every 6 hours, then 25 mg q6h from 14:30 Wed

orders.name: heparin injection (VTE prophylaxis)
orders.instructions: Administer 5,000 units Subcutaneous Every 8 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Platelets fell from 288 to 128 (over 50%) within 48 h in sepsis: HIT unlikely (timing under 5 days and sepsis explains it), team watching.
medication.hold: Hold and call for platelets under 100, new bleeding, or an invasive procedure within 4 h.

orders.name: pantoprazole (PROTONIX) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg IV Daily.

orders.name: chlorhexidine gluconate 0.12% oral rinse
orders.instructions: Administer 15 mL Oropharyngeal Every 12 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Swab teeth and gums; do not swallow. Stops at extubation.

orders.name: acetaminophen (OFIRMEV) IV
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mg IV Every 8 hours.
orders.rationale: Multimodal analgesia (maximum 3 g/day with elevated AST)

medication.importantInfo: Antipyretic effect can mask fever: record temperature BEFORE each dose.
medication.hold: Hold for AST/ALT above 3 times normal; count all acetaminophen sources.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mg Oral Every 8 hours.

orders.name: gabapentin (NEURONTIN) capsule
orders.instructions: Administer 300 mg Oral Three times daily.

medication.importantInfo: Causes sedation and dizziness: fall risk. Adjust for creatinine clearance.

orders.name: hydromorphone (DILAUDID) injection
orders.frequency: Every 3 hours as needed for CPOT 4 or higher / before dressing changes
orders.instructions: Give 15 minutes before dressing changes and for CPOT 4 or higher despite the fentanyl infusion. Max 3 mg/4 h.

medication.freqKey: Every 3 hours as needed for CPOT 4 or higher / before dressing changes

orders.name: oxycodone (ROXICODONE) tablet
orders.frequency: Every 4 hours as needed (5 mg for pain 4-6; 10 mg for pain 7-10)
orders.instructions: Administer 5-10 mg Oral Every 4 hours as needed (5 mg for pain 4-6; 10 mg for pain 7-10).

medication.freqKey: Every 4 hours as needed (5 mg for pain 4-6; 10 mg for pain 7-10)
medication.hold: Hold for sedation (RASS -2 or lower) or RR under 10.

orders.name: lorazepam (ATIVAN) injection
orders.frequency: Once as needed for severe agitation
orders.instructions: Administer 1 mg IV Once as needed for severe agitation.
orders.rationale: Severe agitation, ETT biting; benzodiazepines increase delirium: use sparingly

medication.freqKey: Once as needed for severe agitation

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection
orders.frequency: Every 8 hours as needed for nausea
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 8 hours as needed for nausea.

medication.freqKey: Every 8 hours as needed for nausea
medication.hold: Check QTc if on other QT-prolonging drugs.

orders.name: senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 2 tablets Oral (per OG tube) Twice daily.

orders.name: ascorbic acid (vitamin C) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mg Oral (per OG tube) Twice daily.
orders.rationale: Wound healing and burn antioxidant therapy

orders.name: zinc sulfate capsule
orders.instructions: Administer 220 mg Oral (per OG tube) Daily.
orders.rationale: Wound healing, burn trace element losses

orders.name: multivitamin with minerals tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 tablet Oral (per OG tube) Daily.

orders.name: thiamine 100 mg and folic acid 1 mg tablets
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mg / 1 mg Oral (per OG tube) Daily.
orders.rationale: Alcohol use history (4-6 beers on weekends, more tonight), refeeding risk

orders.name: potassium chloride 20 mEq in 100 mL
orders.instructions: Central line only, 10 mEq/h maximum, on telemetry. Recheck K 4 hours after.

orders.name: magnesium sulfate 2 g in 50 mL
orders.instructions: Administer 2 g IV Once.

orders.name: sodium phosphate 15 mmol in 250 mL
orders.instructions: Administer 15 mmol IV (central line) Once.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale
orders.frequency: Every 6 hours while NPO, then before meals and at bedtime
orders.instructions: Glucose 151-200: 2 units; 201-250: 4 units; 251-300: 6 units; 301-350: 8 units; over 350: 10 units and call provider. Under 70: treat per hypoglycemia protocol.

medication.importantInfo: Check glucose first. Call provider for glucose under 70 or over 350.
medication.freqKey: Every 6 hours while NPO, then before meals and at bedtime

orders.name: albuterol nebulizer (inhalation injury protocol)
orders.instructions: Administer 2.5 mg Inhalation (in-line) Every 4 hours.

orders.name: heparin 5,000 units nebulized (inhalation injury protocol)
orders.instructions: Administer 5,000 units in 3 mL saline Inhalation (in-line) Every 8 hours (alternates with acetylcysteine).
orders.rationale: Reduces airway cast formation after smoke inhalation

orders.name: acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL nebulized (inhalation injury protocol)
orders.instructions: Administer 3 mL Inhalation (in-line) Every 8 hours (alternates with heparin).
orders.rationale: Thins secretions and casts after smoke inhalation

medication.importantInfo: Can cause bronchospasm: give with albuterol; suction after treatment.

orders.name: silver sulfadiazine 1% cream (SILVADENE)
orders.instructions: Administer Thin layer 1/16 inch Topical Daily with dressing change.
orders.rationale: Burn wound care chest and right arm

medication.importantInfo: Replaced by mafenide at 16:45 Tue after wound exam.

orders.name: mafenide acetate 5% solution soaks (SULFAMYLON)
orders.instructions: Administer Soak dressings, keep moist Topical Every 8 hours.
orders.rationale: Early burn wound infection, penetrates eschar

medication.importantInfo: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor: can cause metabolic acidosis and is painful on application. Premedicate for pain.

orders.name: bacitracin ointment (face)
orders.instructions: Administer Thin layer Topical Twice daily.

orders.name: NPO (tube feeding only)
orders.instructions: Nothing by mouth; enteral nutrition via OG tube only.

orders.name: Osmolite 1.5 tube feeding via OG tube
orders.instructions: Start 20 mL/h at 10:00; advance 10 mL/h every 4 hours to goal 70 mL/h (about 2,500 kcal, 105 g protein). Check residuals every 4 h (hold feeds and call for over 500 mL). Free water flush 30 mL every 4 hours. HOB 30 degrees or higher. Do NOT hold feeds for dressing changes (hold only for OR or extubation).
orders.rationale: Early enteral nutrition for burns over 20% reduces hypermetabolic response
nursing: Advance rate per protocol and chart the rate
Glucose every hour on the insulin infusion: when feeds are held, call before changing insulin

orders.name: Soft diet with high-protein oral supplements
orders.instructions: Soft diet, aspiration precautions, upright for meals, ensure-type supplement TID. Dietitian following.

orders.name: Bed rest, HOB at 30 degrees or higher; right arm elevated above heart level
orders.instructions: Position of function with the right hand splinted. Turn side to side every 2 hours without lying on the burned right arm or chest. Fall precautions after extubation.

orders.name: Out of bed to chair with PT/OT and nursing
orders.instructions: Dangle then chair with 2 assist, ETT removed, monitor SpO2 and HR.

orders.name: Mechanical ventilation: AC/VC, VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW), RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 titrate to SpO2 92% or higher
orders.instructions: Low tidal volume ventilation: VT 6 mL/kg ideal body weight (IBW 75 kg = 450 mL). Keep plateau under 30. SpO2 goal 94% or higher while COHb elevated, then 92%+. Daily SBT when FiO2 0.40 or less and PEEP 5-8.
nursing: Oral care with chlorhexidine every 12 h
Suction only when clinically indicated; document secretions

orders.name: Spontaneous breathing trial (daily)
orders.instructions: PS 5 / PEEP 5 / FiO2 0.35 for 30 minutes. Pass: RR under 30, SpO2 92% or higher, HR change under 20%, RSBI under 105, no distress. Cuff leak test before extubation.

orders.name: Oxygen via nasal cannula titrate SpO2 92% or higher
orders.instructions: After extubation: 4 L/min, wean to 2 L, then room air for SpO2 92% or higher. Incentive spirometry every hour while awake; cough and deep breathing.

orders.name: Burn resuscitation: hourly urine output, titrate fluids per Parkland protocol
orders.instructions: Strict hourly I&O via Foley. Goal UOP 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h = 41 mL/h). Adjust LR per order. Call burn team for UOP under 20 mL/h x1 or over 100 mL/h.
nursing: Weigh at admission only (bed scale) then daily at 05:00

orders.name: Neurovascular and compartment checks right arm and hand
orders.frequency: Every hour x24 h then every 2 hours
orders.instructions: Doppler or palpable radial/ulnar pulses, capillary refill, color, temperature, sensation and motion of fingers (when able), tension of forearm. Call burn team immediately for loss of Doppler signal, pallor, increasing pain or tense forearm.

orders.name: Sedation and pain scales: RASS and CPOT every hour; RASS goal per day
orders.instructions: RASS goal -2 to -3 Monday, -1 to -2 Tuesday, 0 to -1 Wednesday. CPOT every hour, treat 4 or higher. CAM-ICU every shift when RASS -3 or higher.

orders.name: Daily sedation interruption (SAT) with RN and RT at 08:00
orders.instructions: Hold propofol; fentanyl continues unchanged for pain. Wake to RASS 0 to -1 or until agitation or distress, then restart at half the prior rate. Pair with SBT when criteria are met.

orders.name: Intra-abdominal (bladder) pressure every 6 hours
orders.instructions: Measure via Foley port (25 mL saline, end-expiration). Call for pressure over 15 mmHg.

orders.name: Burn wound care and dressing changes daily
orders.instructions: Daily at 14:00 with burn nurse. Pre-medicate 15 min before. Gown, gloves, mask, sterile technique. Assess wound edges, drainage, odor, eschar, surrounding erythema. Photograph and measure. Mark margin of any spreading erythema with skin marker.

orders.name: Hourly vital signs and arterial line monitoring
orders.instructions: Level and zero the transducer at the phlebostatic axis each shift and after position changes. Pressure bag 300 mmHg. Check right hand perfusion distal to the line is not applicable: left radial line, assess left hand every 2 hours.

orders.name: Turn every 2 hours, pressure injury prevention, heel offloading
orders.instructions: Avoid positioning on the burned chest/right arm. Use low air loss mattress. Braden every shift.

orders.name: Soft wrist restraint, left wrist (safe ETT and line protection)
orders.frequency: Renew every 24 h, assess every 2 h
orders.instructions: Per policy: attending order required each calendar day, circulation check every 2 hours. Remove at extubation.

orders.name: Bowel regimen and stool chart
orders.instructions: Chart stool character and volume. Hold laxative for loose stools; send C. difficile test for 3 or more loose stools in 24 h.

orders.name: Foley catheter care and daily necessity review
orders.instructions: Maintain closed system, securement device, catheter care each shift. Remove when hourly urine output no longer required (burn team decision).

orders.name: Central line care: chlorhexidine dressing change every 7 days, scrub the hub 15 seconds
orders.instructions: Check site each shift. Daily line necessity review. Culture and call provider for fever with a central line.

orders.name: Aspiration precautions after extubation, swallow screen before oral intake
orders.instructions: Nothing by mouth until the bedside swallow screen is passed. Upright 90 degrees to eat.

orders.name: Point-of-care glucose every 6 hours; hourly on the insulin infusion
orders.instructions: Hourly while on insulin infusion, per protocol table. Treat glucose under 70 with D50 per protocol.

orders.name: Arterial blood gas with lactate every 4 hours, then per ICU team
orders.instructions: q4h x24 h, then q6-8h; extra gases with ventilator changes and clinical change.

orders.name: BMP, magnesium and phosphorus every 6 hours x24 h, then every 12 hours
CBC every 12 hours; coagulation panel daily
Sepsis labs: lactate, procalcitonin, blood cultures x2 (peripheral and central line), wound culture, tracheal aspirate, urine culture
orders.instructions: Draw cultures BEFORE antibiotics; wound swab from the area of purulent drainage after cleansing. Lactate repeat in 2 hours if over 2.

orders.name: Repeat blood cultures x2 (peripheral and central line)
orders.instructions: Draw before the next antibiotic dose, different sites.

orders.name: Chest x-ray daily at 05:00 and after any line or tube placement
orders.instructions: ETT 3-5 cm above the carina; line tips; infiltrates.

orders.name: Contact precautions (burn unit)
orders.instructions: Gown and gloves for all wound care and room entry; dedicated equipment.

orders.name: Fall precautions
orders.instructions: After extubation: bed low, call light in reach, assist x2, non-skid footwear.

orders.name: Registered dietitian consult
orders.instructions: Nutrition assessment within 24 hours, hypermetabolic burn.

orders.name: PT / OT consult (burn rehabilitation)
orders.instructions: Positioning, splints, range of motion; mobilization when safe.

orders.name: Infectious Diseases consult
orders.instructions: Burn wound infection with positive blood culture (GPC in clusters).

orders.name: Case management and social work consult
orders.instructions: Family support, insurance, disposition planning.

orders.name: Full Code
orders.instructions: Full resuscitation.

stickyNotes.title: Burn resuscitation
stickyNotes.body: Parkland 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR in 24 h from injury (01:30). Half by 09:30, half over the next 16 h. Titrate hourly to UOP 30-50 mL/h. Over-resuscitation (fluid creep) is a risk.

stickyNotes.title: Airway / inhalation injury
stickyNotes.body: Intubated 02:50 (8.0 ETT, 24 cm). COHb was 14.2% (pulse ox reads falsely normal). Facial burns and swelling: do not retape the ETT without help.

stickyNotes.title: Right arm
stickyNotes.body: Circumferential burn with escharotomy at 03:15. Elevate above heart level. Check Doppler pulses, cap refill, color and tension EVERY hour.

stickyNotes.title: Burn wound infection / sepsis
stickyNotes.body: Right arm and chest wound infection with sepsis (MSSA): fever 102.4 F, HR to 132, norepinephrine up to 0.14 mcg/kg/min, lactate peak 4.1. Mafenide soaks q8h. Cultures drawn 15:50 Tue. Watch MAP, UOP, glucose and wound margin.

notes.title: EMS Handoff Summary
notes.author: K. Ruiz, Paramedic (Medic 4)
notes.summary: 34 M, house fire victim with flame burns and smoke inhalation, 500 mL LR and high-flow O2 given en route, handed off to ED at 02:30.
notes.body:
**Dispatch and Times**
- Call received 01:38 for structure fire with reported injured occupant. Medic 4 on scene 01:55, patient contact 02:00, left scene 02:14, arrived ED 02:30. Transfer of care to A. Torres, RN and Dr. Castellano at 02:30.

**Scene and Mechanism**
- Single-family house fire, estimated time of injury 01:30. Patient is a 34-year-old male who per his partner fell asleep on the couch after drinking alcohol and smoking, woke to heavy smoke, and went back into the enclosed, smoke-filled house to carry his 6-year-old daughter out. He was found by firefighters on the front lawn outside the structure, coughing and sitting upright. Partner (Jenna Whitaker) and daughter (Ava) were outside and uninjured; a second unit evaluated them and transported them to the ED for observation.
- Flame burns to right arm and anterior chest. Prolonged exposure to smoke in an enclosed space. No fall, no blunt trauma, no loss of consciousness per witnesses. Spinal motion restriction not indicated.

**Primary Assessment**
- Airway: hoarse voice, soot around nares and mouth, singed nasal hairs, productive cough with black sputum. No stridor at scene contact; mild inspiratory noise noted en route.
- Breathing: tachypneic, bilateral wheezes and scattered rhonchi. Circulation: radial pulses present left, weak right hand. Disability: GCS 15, alert and oriented, smells of alcohol, anxious. Exposure: burns as below.

**Vital Signs**
- 02:03: HR 126, BP 142/86, RR 26, SpO2 94% room air. After NRB 15 L/min: SpO2 99%.
- 02:25: HR 120, BP 136/82, RR 24, SpO2 99% on NRB. Glucose 138 mg/dL. Cardiac monitor sinus tachycardia, no ectopy. Temp not obtained.

**Burn Assessment**
- Estimated 20% TBSA by rule of nines: right arm circumferential (approx 9%), anterior chest (approx 9%), face and neck. Right forearm and hand appear leathery and white; right hand swollen. Pain 8/10.

**Treatment**
- 100% O2 by non-rebreather mask 15 L/min from 02:03 (carbon monoxide exposure suspected).
- IV 20 g left hand. Lactated Ringer's 500 mL infused en route (documented 02:20).
- Burned areas covered with dry sterile burn sheets; no creams or wet dressings applied. Jewelry removed from right hand. Kept warm with blankets.
- No analgesics given prehospital (short transport, airway concern).

**Handoff**
- Report given to ED: concern for inhalation injury and impending airway compromise; patient alert and protecting airway at handoff. Belongings given to partner.

notes.title: Procedure Note: Endotracheal Intubation
notes.author: M. Castellano, MD
notes.summary: RSI with etomidate and rocuronium, 8.0 ETT placed at 24 cm at 02:50 for inhalation injury with impending airway obstruction.
notes.body:
**Procedure**
Emergent orotracheal intubation, rapid sequence induction.

**Indication**
Inhalation injury with facial burns, hoarse voice, developing stridor, singed nasal hair and oropharyngeal soot. High risk of progressive airway edema as resuscitation fluids begin.

**Consent and Time-out**
Emergent, implied consent; patient alert but airway at risk. Time-out performed with A. Torres, RN and RT.

**Preparation**
- Preoxygenation with 100% O2 by NRB for more than 3 minutes. Monitor: HR 122, BP 128/78 (MAP 95), SpO2 100% (not reliable, COHb pending). Suction, bougie, video laryngoscope and surgical airway kit at bedside. Two smaller ETT sizes available given expected edema. No cervical spine concern (no trauma).

**Medications (02:50)**
Etomidate 20 mg IV, rocuronium 100 mg IV.

**Technique**
Direct laryngoscopy with a Macintosh blade. Grade 2 view with edematous, erythematous supraglottic mucosa and soot. First pass success. 8.0 cuffed ETT placed 24 cm at the teeth. Cuff inflated to 24 cm H2O.

**Confirmation**
Positive waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds, symmetric chest rise, condensation in the tube. SpO2 remained 100% throughout; no desaturation, hypotension or arrhythmia. Tube secured with commercial holder. Black sooty secretions suctioned.

**Initial Ventilator Settings**
AC/VC VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW), RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0. PIP 28, Pplat 21.

**Post-intubation**
Propofol infusion and fentanyl ordered for sedation. OG tube being placed. Portable CXR ordered to confirm ETT position (tip to be 3-5 cm above the carina).

**Complications**
None. Estimated blood loss none.

notes.title: Portable Chest X-ray, Post-intubation
notes.author: Radiology Department
notes.summary: ETT 4 cm above the carina, OG tube in stomach, lungs clear with mild perihilar haze.
notes.body:
**Exam**
Portable AP chest radiograph, supine, 03:20.

**Indication**
Post-intubation and OG tube placement; inhalation injury.

**Comparison**
None.

**Findings**
- Endotracheal tube tip 4 cm above the carina. Orogastric tube courses below the diaphragm with the tip in the stomach. ECG leads and burn dressings overlie the chest.
- Lungs are clear. Mild perihilar haziness bilaterally. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax.
- Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal. No acute osseous abnormality.
notes.impression: ETT tip 4 cm above carina in good position. OG tube tip in stomach. Lungs clear with mild perihilar haze; no pneumothorax.

notes.title: Procedure Note: Escharotomy, Right Forearm and Hand
notes.author: R. Okafor, MD
notes.summary: Bedside escharotomy of the right forearm and hand at 03:15 for compartment-like findings; Doppler signals returned; chest escharotomy not needed.
notes.body:
**Procedure**
Bedside escharotomy, right forearm and hand.

**Indication**
Circumferential full-thickness burn of the right forearm and hand with a tense forearm, absent Doppler signals to the hand and increasing pain, concerning for compartment syndrome and vascular compromise from unyielding eschar during resuscitation.

**Consent**
Emergent; patient intubated and sedated. Partner Jenna Whitaker informed at bedside.

**Technique**
Sterile prep and drape with chlorhexidine, patient sedated on propofol and fentanyl with additional fentanyl given by the ED team. Mid-lateral and mid-medial incisions were made through the eschar with electrocautery, down to viable subcutaneous tissue, from the proximal forearm across the wrist and onto the hand, then along the thenar and hypothenar regions. Digits were not incised. Eschar edges released with immediate visible gaping and softening of the forearm.

**Findings and Result**
- Forearm compartments soft after release. Doppler signals returned at the radial and ulnar arteries and palmar arch, and signals present in the digits. Cap refill under 3 seconds.
- Bleeding about 150 mL, controlled with electrocautery and pressure. Vitals during the case: HR 112-116, BP 110/68 (MAP 82) at 03:20.

**Dressing and Aftercare**
- Incisions dressed with non-adherent gauze and loose wrap, fingertips left visible. Hand splinted in position of function and the arm elevated above heart level on pillows.
- Neurovascular checks (Doppler signal, cap refill, color, warmth, tension) hourly; call burn team immediately for loss of Doppler signal, pallor, tense forearm or escalating pain.

**Chest**
Anterior chest burn reviewed. Escharotomy not required: burn is anterior only, ventilation is adequate with PIP 28 and no restrictive chest wall findings. Will reassess if PIP rises.

**Complications**
None. Tolerated well.

**Plan**
Admit Burn ICU. Full burn H&P to follow.

notes.title: ED Provider Note
notes.author: M. Castellano, MD
notes.summary: ED course for a 34 M with 22% TBSA flame burns and inhalation injury: intubated 02:50, escharotomy 03:15, resuscitation started, admitted to Burn ICU.
notes.body:
**Chief Complaint**
Burns to right arm, chest and face after house fire; smoke inhalation.

**HPI**
34-year-old male, arrived by EMS 02:30 after a house fire (injury about 01:30). He fell asleep on the couch after drinking and smoking, woke to smoke and re-entered to carry his 6-year-old daughter out; found outside by firefighters. Received O2 by NRB and LR 500 mL from EMS. PMH childhood asthma (resolved), seasonal allergies. Meds: cetirizine PRN. NKDA. Tobacco 1 ppd x 15 years, alcohol on weekends, no drugs. Tdap unknown, more than 10 years ago.

**Primary Survey (02:30-02:35)**
- A: hoarse voice, soot in oropharynx and nares, singed nasal hair, facial burns, early inspiratory stridor developing. B: RR 24, wheezes and rhonchi, SpO2 99% on NRB (unreliable with CO exposure). C: HR 118, BP 138/84 (MAP 102), cap refill about 3 sec right hand. D: GCS 15. E: temp 96.8 F, warmed.

**Secondary Survey**
- Right arm circumferential burn, forearm and hand leathery full thickness, upper arm deep partial; anterior chest deep partial with full-thickness patches; face and neck superficial to partial. Bilateral corneas clear with fluorescein. TBSA 22% (confirmed with Dr. Okafor), about 8% full thickness. No other injuries.

**Airway Decision**
Hoarseness, developing stridor, singed nasal hair, soot and facial burns indicate high risk for rapid upper airway edema. Decision for early definitive airway. RSI at 02:50 with etomidate 20 mg and rocuronium 100 mg; 8.0 ETT placed, 24 cm at the teeth, direct laryngoscopy, grade 2 view with edema (see procedure note). Placed on AC/VC 450/16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0. Post-intubation HR 116, BP 116/72 at 03:05.

**Studies**
- 02:40 labs: WBC 12.8, Hgb 17.2, Plt 288, Na 138, K 4.3, CO2 19, Cr 0.9, glucose 143, lactate 5.8 (02:50), ethanol 42 mg/dL, INR 1.1, troponin I 0.02, CK 480. UDS negative. UA dark amber, SG 1.031, myoglobin negative.
- ABG 02:50 (on 100% O2): pH 7.29, PaCO2 38, PaO2 412, HCO3 18, BE -7, COHb 14.2%. Pulse oximeter overestimates saturation in CO poisoning.
- Cyanide considered given lactate 5.8 and soot exposure; patient hemodynamically stable with intact mentation, so hydroxocobalamin not given; lactate to be rechecked after fluids.

**Resuscitation**
- Parkland: 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR in 24 h from injury (01:30). Half (3,608 mL) in the first 8 h (to 09:30), remainder over the next 16 h. EMS 500 mL counted; remaining 3,108 mL over 7 h is about 444 mL/h. LR started 02:30 at 450 mL/h, titrate to UOP 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h).
- Left AC 18 g PIV 02:40. Foley 02:45 (dark amber urine). OG tube 16 Fr 03:05. Left IJ triple-lumen CVC placed 03:45 under ultrasound (see procedure note).

**Medications**
- Fentanyl 100 mcg IV 02:36, infusion 50 mcg/h from 03:00, bolus 100 mcg at 03:12, infusion increased to 100 mcg/h at 03:40. Propofol started 02:55. Albuterol 2.5 mg neb 02:45. Tdap 0.5 mL IM 03:30.

**Burn Surgery**
Dr. Okafor called 02:55, at bedside 03:10. Right forearm tense with absent Doppler signals to the hand and pain: bedside escharotomy at 03:15 with return of Doppler signals (see his note). Chest ventilation adequate, PIP 28, escharotomy not needed.

**Imaging**
Portable CXR 03:20: ETT 4 cm above carina, OG in stomach, lungs clear to mild perihilar haze.

**Vitals at 03:55**
HR 110, BP 104/62 (MAP 76), RR 18 (vent), SpO2 100%, temp 97.2 F, CPOT 2/8, RASS -3.

**Assessment and Disposition**
22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury and CO poisoning, acute respiratory failure s/p intubation, burn shock. Admitted to Burn ICU under Dr. Okafor with intensivist Dr. Brandt co-managing. Full code. Partner Jenna Whitaker updated at bedside. Report to ICU RN and transport to the Burn ICU at 04:00 on monitor with RT.

notes.title: Procedure Note: Central Venous Catheter, Left IJ
notes.author: M. Castellano, MD
notes.summary: Ultrasound-guided left IJ 7 Fr triple-lumen CVC placed at 03:45 under full barrier precautions; CXR to confirm tip.
notes.body:
**Procedure**
Central venous catheter placement, left internal jugular vein, 7 Fr triple lumen.

**Indication**
Large-volume burn resuscitation (22% TBSA), burned right arm limiting peripheral access, possible need for vasoactive infusions and sedation drips.

**Consent**
Emergent; patient sedated and intubated.

**Technique**
- Site chosen at the left neck where skin is unburned (right neck and anterior chest burned). Time-out done. Hand hygiene, sterile full-barrier precautions (cap, mask, sterile gown and gloves, full body drape). Chlorhexidine skin prep, allowed to dry.
- Ultrasound with sterile probe cover: left IJ vein patent, compressible, lateral to carotid. Local lidocaine 1% 4 mL. Real-time ultrasound-guided needle entry on first pass with dark nonpulsatile blood return, guidewire advanced without resistance (no ectopy on monitor), skin nick, dilation, catheter advanced over the wire to 16 cm at the skin.
- All three lumens aspirate blood and flush easily. Sutured in place with chlorhexidine-impregnated dressing, line date on dressing.

**Findings**
Blood return from all lumens. No arrhythmia. Estimated blood loss under 5 mL. Vitals during procedure: HR 112, BP 106/64 (MAP 78), SpO2 100%.

**Confirmation**
Portable chest x-ray ordered for tip position and pneumothorax before use of the catheter for vasoactive or hyperosmolar infusions. Ultrasound of the lung showed lung sliding bilaterally.

**Complications**
None apparent.

**Plan**
CXR to confirm; central line care bundle; daily necessity review. Patient to Burn ICU.
