notes.title: Nursing Note - ICU Arrival / Admission
notes.author: E. Haddad, RN
notes.summary: Admission to BICU-6 from ED with bedside handoff and full head-to-toe assessment; Parkland LR 450 mL/h, goal UOP 30-50 mL/h.
notes.body:
**Handoff**
- Arrived BICU-6 at 04:00 from ED with A. Torres, RN. Bedside SBAR handoff and two-identifier check done (name/DOB, MRN SIM-40101). 34 y/o M, 82 kg, flame burn 22% TBSA + smoke inhalation from house fire ~01:30. NKDA. Full Code. Admit orders (04:10) verified against handoff.
- ED course: EMS LR 500 mL; L AC PIV 02:40; Foley 02:45; intubated 02:50; OG 03:05; R forearm/hand escharotomy 03:15; Tdap 03:30; L IJ CVC 03:45. COHb 14.2% (02:50) -> 6.4% (04:15); lactate 5.8 -> 3.4. Dr. Brandt performed bedside bronchoscopy 04:20: grade 2 inhalation injury (erythema, soot, mucosal edema), ETT left in place.

**Vitals (04:00)**
- HR 106 ST, BP 101/58 (MAP 72), RR 17, SpO2 100% (falsely reassuring with elevated COHb), T 97.4 °F bladder. POC glucose 148.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: sedated, RASS -3 (goal -2 to -3) on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min + fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils 3 mm, equal, brisk. Does not follow commands; withdraws L arm to stimulus. CPOT 1/8.
- Resp: 8.0 oral ETT 24 cm at teeth, secured. AC/VC VT 450, set RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0; PIP 28/Pplat 21. BS coarse with scattered rhonchi bilaterally, no wheeze. Small black-flecked carbonaceous secretions on suction; perioral soot, singed nasal hairs.
- CV: ST, no ectopy. Generalized edema starting. L radial 2+, cap refill 2 s L hand. R hand: Doppler radial and ulnar signals present and strong after escharotomy (marked with skin marker); exposed nail beds warm.
- GI: OG 16 Fr to low intermittent suction, 30 mL green-clear; abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds hypoactive x4. NPO.
- GU: Foley 16 Fr with temp probe, dark amber urine (SG 1.031 on ED UA, myoglobin negative); ED-reported UOP ~25 mL/h.
- Skin: R arm circumferential 9% - forearm/hand full-thickness (waxy, leathery, insensate), upper arm deep partial (mottled, weeping). Anterior chest 9% deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches. Face/neck 4% superficial to superficial partial (erythema, small blisters). Total 22% TBSA (~8% full-thickness). Escharotomy incisions dressed, minimal ooze. R arm on pillows above heart, hand splinted in position of function. Back/legs intact.
- Lines: L IJ triple-lumen CVC (tip at cavo-atrial junction per CXR), CHG dressing intact; L AC 18 g PIV patent, no infiltration. Arterial line to be placed by Dr. Brandt.

**Resuscitation**
- Parkland 4 x 82 x 22 = 7,216 mL/24 h from 01:30 (3,608 mL in first 8 h, EMS 500 mL counted). LR 450 mL/h via CVC. Hourly UOP goal 30-50 mL/h (41 mL/h = 0.5 mL/kg/h); notify burn team if <30 mL/h x2 h or <20 mL/h.

**Safety / family**
- Soft L wrist restraint (ETT/line protection), skin intact, restraint order requested; contact precautions; suction, BVM at bedside; HOB 30; low air loss mattress.
- Jenna Whitaker (partner) at bedside, updated and oriented to unit, visiting rules, gown/glove. Clothing not salvageable; wallet/phone and ring (removed in ED) given to Jenna. Daughter Ava is safe with family.

notes.title: Procedure Note: Arterial Line, Left Radial
notes.author: L. Brandt, MD
notes.summary: Left radial 20 g arterial line placed at 04:30 for continuous BP and frequent ABGs.
notes.body:
**Procedure**
Arterial catheter placement, left radial artery, 20 gauge.

**Indication**
Hemodynamic monitoring during burn resuscitation with expected hypermetabolic changes and edema (noninvasive cuff unreliable), q4h arterial blood gases and lactate, mechanical ventilation.

**Consent**
Emergent/implied; patient sedated. Partner informed at bedside.

**Technique**
Right arm is burned, so the left was used. Modified Allen test normal (palmar flush within 5 seconds with ulnar compression). Time-out performed. Wrist positioned in dorsiflexion, chlorhexidine prep, sterile gloves and drape, lidocaine 1% 1 mL local. 20 g catheter placed at 04:30 with pulsatile flash on the first attempt, advanced over the wire. Connected to pressure tubing with 300 mmHg pressure bag, transducer leveled and zeroed at the phlebostatic axis. Sutured and dressed.

**Findings**
Good arterial waveform, no dampening. Arterial pressure correlates with cuff pressure (MAP about 70-72 mmHg). Left hand pink, warm, cap refill under 2 seconds; no ischemic changes after placement.

**Complications**
None; minimal bleeding.

**Plan**
Check left hand perfusion every 2 hours; zero and level each shift and with position change; daily necessity review. Draw q4h ABG and lactate from line.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Arterial Line and Hourly Neurovascular Check
notes.author: E. Haddad, RN
notes.summary: L radial arterial line placed 04:30 by Dr. Brandt, waveform and zeroing verified; hourly R hand Doppler check unchanged; UOP 25 mL for 04-05.
notes.body:
**Arterial line**
- L radial 20 g arterial line placed 04:30 by Dr. Brandt (R arm burned). Modified Allen test normal pre-procedure. Sterile technique with full barrier and CHG prep; secured with sutures, transparent dressing and arm board, site clean/dry, no hematoma.
- Transducer leveled and zeroed to air at the phlebostatic axis. Pressure bag 300 mmHg, flush running. Waveform crisp with dicrotic notch; fast-flush square wave test acceptable (not over- or underdamped). Art BP 99/55 (MAP 70) correlates with NIBP L arm within 5 mmHg. First ABG drawn from line without difficulty.
- L hand checked q2h for line complications: warm, pink, cap refill 2 s, normal motion/sensation not assessable (sedated), no blanching.

**Hourly R arm/hand neurovascular check (05:00)**
- Doppler: radial and ulnar signals present, strong biphasic, unchanged from 04:00. Digital signals present digits 2-5.
- Forearm soft and compressible above and below the escharotomy; incisions open with minimal serosanguineous ooze. Fingertips warm, no pallor, no cyanosis. Cap refill in exposed nail beds ~3 s (burn edema). No new tension. Arm elevated on pillows above heart; splint intact, not constricting.
- Burn team to be called immediately for loss of Doppler signal, pallor, tense forearm or escalating pain response.

**Other**
- Vitals 05:00: HR 109 ST, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 18, SpO2 99%, T 97.6 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. PIP 28/Pplat 21, FiO2 1.0.
- I&O 04:00-05:00: in 537 mL, UOP 25 mL (0.30 mL/kg/h), dark amber - below 30 mL/h goal for the first hour. LR continues 450 mL/h. Will re-evaluate at 06:00 and call the burn team if UOP remains below 30 mL/h for a second consecutive hour.
- 06:00 labs and ABG due; heparin SQ and acetaminophen IV also due 06:00.

notes.title: Procedure Note: Bronchoscopy
notes.author: L. Brandt, MD
notes.summary: Bronchoscopy through ETT at 04:20 shows grade 2 inhalation injury; airway cleared and inhalation injury protocol started.
notes.body:
**Procedure**
Flexible fiberoptic bronchoscopy through the endotracheal tube, performed at 04:20.

**Indication**
Evaluation and grading of inhalation injury after enclosed-space fire exposure, soot in the airway; pulmonary toilet.

**Sedation and Monitoring**
On propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h, RASS -3. FiO2 1.0 maintained throughout. HR 106, BP 101/58 (MAP 72), SpO2 100%. Airway pressures monitored.

**Findings**
- ETT 24 cm at the teeth, tip about 4 cm above the carina. Vocal cords edematous; supraglottic mucosal erythema and edema.
- Trachea and mainstem bronchi: diffuse erythema, soot deposition and mucosal edema. No ulceration or mucosal sloughing. No carbonaceous casts below the carina. Thick sooty secretions in the trachea and right mainstem bronchus.
- Abbreviated Injury Score grade 2 (mild-moderate) inhalation injury.

**Intervention**
Sooty secretions suctioned and the airway cleared with saline lavage aliquots. No culture sent (no sign of infection). Scope withdrawn without complication.

**Post-procedure**
PIP unchanged at 28, Pplat 21, SpO2 100%.

**Inhalation Injury Protocol Started**
- Albuterol 2.5 mg neb q4h.
- Nebulized heparin 5,000 units q8h alternating every 4 hours with nebulized N-acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL q8h.
- Chest physiotherapy and pulmonary toilet with frequent suctioning. Head of bed 30 degrees.

**Plan**
Continue lung-protective ventilation; wean FiO2 as COHb clears. Repeat bronchoscopy only if clinical change.

notes.title: Burn Surgery History and Physical
notes.author: R. Okafor, MD
notes.summary: Burn surgery admission H&P: 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, post-escharotomy, Parkland resuscitation in progress.
notes.body:
**Chief Complaint**
Flame burns and smoke inhalation after a house fire.

**HPI**
34-year-old right-hand-dominant male HVAC technician. At about 01:30 Monday he fell asleep on the couch after drinking and smoking, woke to smoke and re-entered the enclosed house to carry his 6-year-old daughter out. He sustained flame burns to the right arm and chest and inhaled smoke. Found outside by firefighters. EMS gave O2 and 500 mL LR. In the ED (arrival 02:30) he was hoarse with stridor, soot and singed nasal hair, and was intubated at 02:50. COHb 14.2%. Right forearm escharotomy at 03:15 for tense forearm and absent hand Doppler signals; signals returned. Left IJ CVC 03:45, left radial arterial line 04:30, bronchoscopy 04:20 showed grade 2 inhalation injury. Tdap given 03:30. ICU arrival 04:00.

**PMH / PSH**
Childhood asthma (resolved, no inhalers as an adult), seasonal allergies. No prior surgeries.

**Medications / Allergies**
Cetirizine PRN only. No known drug allergies.

**Social**
Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker (health care proxy discussed) and daughter Ava, 6, both uninjured. Alcohol 4-6 beers on weekends, more on the night of injury (ethanol 42 mg/dL at 02:40). Tobacco 1 ppd x 15 years (15 pack-years). No illicit drugs; urine drug screen negative.

**Review of Systems**
Unobtainable, intubated and sedated. Per ED history no chest pain prior to the fire.

**Vitals (05:00)**
HR 109, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 18 (vent), SpO2 99% (not reliable with COHb), temp 97.6 F, weight 82 kg, height 180 cm.

**Exam**
- General: intubated, sedated, RASS -3. HEENT: facial burns, singed brows and nasal hair, perioral soot, lips edematous. Neck: ETT secured. Lungs: coarse bilateral breath sounds, PIP 28. CV: tachycardic, regular. Abdomen: soft, OG tube in place.
- Right hand: Doppler signals present at radial, ulnar and digital arteries after escharotomy; cap refill 2 seconds; forearm soft. Left arm/legs unburned.

**Burn Map (TBSA 22%, about 8% full thickness)**
- Right arm circumferential 9%: forearm and hand full thickness, upper arm deep partial.
- Anterior chest 9%: deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches.
- Face and neck 4%: superficial to superficial-partial.

**Data**
Lactate 5.8 -> 3.4 (04:15). COHb 14.2% -> 6.4% (04:15). ABG 04:15 pH 7.34, PaCO2 40, PaO2 288. Cr 0.9, K 4.3, CK 480, troponin 0.02. CXR 04:10: ETT, OG, left IJ tip cavo-atrial, no pneumothorax.

**Assessment and Resuscitation Plan**
22% TBSA flame burn with grade 2 inhalation injury and CO exposure in burn shock.
- Parkland: 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR in 24 h from injury (01:30 to 01:30 Tuesday). 3,608 mL in the first 8 h (to 09:30); EMS 500 mL counted, so 3,108 mL over 7 h = 444 mL/h; currently 450 mL/h. Second half 3,608 mL over 16 h (225 mL/h from 09:30).
- Titrate to UOP 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h = 41 mL/h). UOP so far 25 mL/h (04:00-05:00); if under 30 for 2 consecutive hours, raise rate 20-25%; if over 50 for 2 hours, reduce. Watch for fluid creep. Bladder pressure q6h.

**Wound Care Plan**
Initial cleansing and first dressing change at 14:00 with burn nurse: silver sulfadiazine 1% to chest and right arm daily; bacitracin ointment to face BID. Hourly neurovascular checks of the right hand. Arm elevated, hand splinted in position of function.

**Other**
- Tetanus: Tdap given 03:30. Nutrition: trophic tube feeds this morning, dietitian consult. Stress ulcer and VTE prophylaxis. Pain/sedation per ICU. Contact precautions.
- OR: excision and autografting of the full-thickness right forearm/hand and chest areas planned in several days once resuscitation is complete; tentatively Friday 11-06.
- Consults: critical care (Dr. Brandt), RD, PT/OT, case management/social work, pharmacy.

**Disposition**
Burn ICU, full code. Plan discussed with Jenna Whitaker at bedside.

notes.title: Respiratory Therapy Initial Evaluation
notes.author: D. Alvarez, RRT
notes.summary: RT initial evaluation: AC/VC with FiO2 1.0, grade 2 inhalation injury, COHb 6.4% on 04:15 ABG, FiO2 weaning plan, inhalation protocol and VAP bundle started.
notes.body:
**Reason for Evaluation**
34 M, 82 kg, 180 cm (IBW 75 kg), intubated 02:50 in ED for inhalation injury with 22% TBSA burns. Arrived Burn ICU 04:00.

**Airway**
Oral 8.0 ETT, 24 cm at the teeth, secured with commercial holder. CXR 04:10: tip 4 cm above carina. Cuff pressure 24 cm H2O (goal 20-30), checked q shift and with tube repositioning. Bronchoscopy 04:20 (Dr. Brandt): grade 2 inhalation injury, soot cleared.

**Ventilator Settings and Mechanics**
- AC/VC, VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW), set RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0. Total RR 17-18.
- PIP 28, Pplat 21 cm H2O; driving pressure 16; static compliance about 28 mL/cmH2O. Plateau under 30 goal met.
- Breath sounds coarse with scattered rhonchi, improved after bronchoscopy and suctioning. Secretions: moderate, thick, black-tinged, decreasing.

**ABG 04:15 (FiO2 1.0)**
pH 7.34, PaCO2 40, PaO2 288, HCO3 21, BE -4, O2 sat 94%, COHb 6.4% (14.2% at 02:50), lactate 3.4. P/F 288. SpO2 on monitor 100% overestimates oxygen content while COHb is elevated; use ABG co-oximetry.

**FiO2 Weaning Plan**
- Keep FiO2 1.0 while COHb is elevated (half-life of COHb about 60-90 min on 100% O2). Order received to wean to 0.60 at 06:00, goal PaO2 80-120 and SpO2 94% or higher; ABG with COHb at 08:00 before further weaning. Continue wean by 0.10 q2-4h as gases allow; target FiO2 0.40 by tomorrow if COHb under 3%.

**Inhalation Injury Protocol**
- Albuterol 2.5 mg neb q4h. Nebulized heparin 5,000 units in 3 mL saline and nebulized N-acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL, each q8h, alternated every 4 hours (heparin 07:00, 15:00, 23:00; NAC 11:00, 19:00, 03:00). Chest physiotherapy and suction q2-4h and PRN.

**VAP Bundle**
- HOB 30 degrees or higher, oral care with chlorhexidine 0.12% BID plus toothbrushing q12h, suction as needed (no subglottic suction ETT), closed in-line suction, daily SAT/SBT assessment, VTE and stress ulcer prophylaxis, circuit changes only if soiled, cuff pressure q shift.

**Plan**
RT to follow q4h with settings check, daily CXR review, SBT screen when FiO2 under 0.50 and PEEP 5-8. Will notify Dr. Brandt for PIP over 35, Pplat over 30, or new secretions.

notes.title: Critical Care Admission History and Physical
notes.author: L. Brandt, MD
notes.summary: ICU admission H&P: 22% TBSA burn with inhalation injury, CO exposure, ventilated respiratory failure and burn shock, plan by system.
notes.body:
**Reason for ICU Admission**
Burn shock and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure after 22% TBSA flame burn with smoke inhalation.

**HPI**
34-year-old male with history of childhood asthma, 15 pack-year smoker, who was injured in a house fire at 01:30 after drinking alcohol. Went back into the house to carry his 6-year-old daughter out. EMS gave 100% O2 and 500 mL LR. ED arrival 02:30: hoarse, stridor, soot; intubated 02:50 (etomidate/rocuronium, 8.0 ETT 24 cm). COHb 14.2%, lactate 5.8, ethanol 42. Right forearm escharotomy 03:15 (burn surgery). Left IJ CVC 03:45, arterial line 04:30, bronchoscopy 04:20: grade 2 inhalation injury. Arrived Burn ICU 04:00. Full code.

**PMH / Meds / Allergies / Social**
Childhood asthma (resolved), seasonal allergies. Cetirizine PRN. NKDA. Alcohol on weekends. Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker (at bedside) and daughter Ava (6, uninjured).

**Vitals (05:00)**
HR 109, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 18 (set 16), SpO2 99%, temp 97.6 F. Vent AC/VC 450/16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0, PIP 28, Pplat 21. LR 450 mL/h. Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. UOP 25 mL/h (04:00-05:00). RASS -3, CPOT 1.

**Exam**
Sedated, RASS -3, no distress. Facial burns and soot, ETT in place. Coarse breath sounds bilaterally, no wheeze now. Tachycardic, regular, cap refill 3 sec. Abdomen soft, nondistended. Right forearm/hand escharotomy incisions dressed, Doppler signals present. No focal neuro deficits (moves left arm and both legs to pain).

**Labs / Imaging**
02:40: WBC 12.8, Hgb 17.2, Plt 288, Na 138, K 4.3, CO2 19, BUN 14, Cr 0.9, glucose 143, INR 1.1, ethanol 42, CK 480, troponin 0.02. ABG 04:15: 7.34/40/288/21, BE -4, COHb 6.4%, lactate 3.4 (5.8 at 02:50). POC glucose 148. CXR 04:10: ETT, OG and left IJ tip cavo-atrial junction good; no PTX; mild bibasilar atelectasis/perihilar haze.

**ICU Problem List**
1. Inhalation injury (grade 2) and CO poisoning.
2. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure on mechanical ventilation.
3. Burn shock / resuscitation.
4. Sedation and analgesia.
5. Hyperglycemia risk / glucose control.
6. VTE prophylaxis.
7. Stress ulcer prophylaxis.
8. Nutrition.
9. Lines and tubes.
10. Alcohol use.

**Assessment and Plan by System**
- Neuro: Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h, RASS goal -2 to -3 today (-1 to -2 Tuesday), CPOT hourly, treat 4 or higher. Daily SAT starting Tuesday. Thiamine/folate for alcohol use; monitor for withdrawal, avoid benzodiazepines when possible.
- Resp: Lung-protective ventilation VT 6 mL/kg IBW (450), Pplat under 30. Wean FiO2 to 0.60 at 06:00; COHb and ABG 08:00; continue 100% O2 until COHb under 3-5%. Inhalation protocol (albuterol, nebulized heparin, NAC), chest PT. HOB 30 degrees, chlorhexidine oral care, daily CXR at 05:00.
- CV/shock: Burn shock with lactate 3.4 (from 5.8). Parkland LR 450 mL/h, titrate to UOP 30-50 mL/h. MAP goal 65 or higher. Cyanide toxicity considered (lactate, soot) but improving with fluids and oxygen; no hydroxocobalamin. Troponin repeat (second troponin due this morning).
- Renal: CK 480; UA myoglobin negative; follow CK x3, BMP/Mg/Phos q6h, bladder pressure q6h.
- GI: OG tube. Trophic feeds Osmolite 1.5 at 20 mL/h at 10:00, advance 10 mL/h q4h to 70 mL/h. Pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily from 09:00.
- Heme: Hgb 17.2 hemoconcentrated; CBC q12h. Heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h (first dose 06:00).
- ID: Tdap given. No prophylactic systemic antibiotics. Topical SSD/bacitracin per burn team.
- Endo: Glucose 143-148; POC q6h, start insulin infusion if persistently over 180.
- Lines: Left IJ CVC (03:45), left radial A-line (04:30), left AC 18 g PIV, OG, Foley (02:45), ETT 24 cm.
- Prophylaxis/Dispo: Burn ICU, full code, contact precautions, family updated.

Critical care time spent: 45 minutes.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Resuscitation Fluid Titration
notes.author: E. Haddad, RN
notes.summary: UOP 25 and 26 mL/h x2 hours; Dr. Okafor called, LR increased 450 to 540 mL/h at 06:00.
notes.body:
**Trigger**
- UOP 04:00-05:00 = 25 mL (0.30 mL/kg/h) and 05:00-06:00 = 26 mL (0.32 mL/kg/h): below the 30 mL/h goal for two consecutive hours per Parkland titration protocol. Urine concentrated, dark amber.

**SBAR to Dr. Okafor (burn surgery), called 05:55**
- S: UOP below goal x2 h on LR 450 mL/h.
- B: 34 y/o M, 22% TBSA flame burn + inhalation injury, 82 kg, Parkland goal 3,608 mL in first 8 h (450 mL/h average from 02:30).
- A: HR 109 ST, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 17, SpO2 100%, T 97.8 °F; lactate 3.4 at 04:15 (down from 5.8). No signs of volume overload; ventilator PIP 28/Pplat 21, unchanged. Bladder pressure checked at 05:30 = 12 mmHg (goal <15). R hand Doppler radial/ulnar signals present, forearm soft, no pallor. Foley patent, no kinks, bladder not distended, flushed per protocol without clot. UA 02:55 myoglobin negative.
- R: increase LR by 20%.
- Order received and read back: LR 450 -> 540 mL/h. Rate changed on the pump with a second RN check at 06:00.

**Reassessment plan**
- Continue hourly UOP, goal 30-50 mL/h (41 mL/h = 0.5 mL/kg/h); recheck at 07:00 and again hourly. If UOP rises above 50 mL/h x2 h the rate will be decreased 20-25%. Notify for UOP <20 mL/h x1, MAP <65, rising PIP/Pplat, bladder pressure >15 mmHg, or any change in R hand signals.
- Soft L wrist restraint order now active (06:00); skin and circulation checked, intact.
- FiO2 weaned from 1.0 to 0.6 at 06:00 by RT (COHb 6.4% at 04:15, PaO2 288). 06:00 BMP/Mg/Phos drawn; heparin SQ 5,000 units and acetaminophen 1,000 mg IV given 06:00.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Summary / Handoff to Day RN
notes.author: E. Haddad, RN
notes.summary: Night summary and handoff to day RN: lines, drips, FiO2 0.6, COHb trend, upcoming care.
notes.body:
**Summary 04:00-06:50**
- Admitted from ED 04:00 with grade 2 inhalation injury and 22% TBSA flame burn. Hemodynamically stable on LR alone; no pressors. Vitals 06:00: HR 109 ST, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 17, SpO2 100%, T 97.8 °F (rewarming with warm blankets and warmed room).
- Neuro: RASS -3, CPOT 1/8 on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min + fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils equal, brisk.
- Resp: 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth. AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 weaned 1.0 -> 0.6 at 06:00. PIP 28/Pplat 21. Carbonaceous secretions decreasing. COHb 14.2% (02:50) -> 6.4% (04:15); next ABG/COHb 08:00. Keep SpO2 goal >=94% until COHb normal.

**Lines / drips**
- L IJ CVC: distal LR 540 mL/h, medial propofol, proximal fentanyl. L AC 18 g PIV saline-locked for IV meds. L radial A-line (placed 04:30): waveform good, bag 300 mmHg, zeroed this shift; L hand perfusion normal. OG to LIS; Foley to gravity bag with hourly UOP; contact precautions.

**Fluids**
- LR 450 -> 540 mL/h at 06:00 per Dr. Okafor for UOP 25 and 26 mL/h. UOP 06:00-07:00 pending (goal 30-50). Parkland 7,216 mL/24 h from 01:30; 3,608 mL by 09:30.

**R arm**
- Hourly Doppler checks: radial/ulnar signals present all hours, forearm soft, no pallor. Arm elevated, splint on. Bladder pressure 12 mmHg at 05:30.

**Family / safety**
- Jenna at bedside most of the night, updated, resting in family room. L wrist soft restraint on; skin intact.

**Coming up**
- 07:00 heparin neb; 08:00 ABG with COHb, albuterol neb; 09:00 pantoprazole, vitamins and chlorhexidine; 09:30 Parkland hour 8 - LR rate change expected per Dr. Okafor; trophic feeds anticipated 10:00; 12:00 labs incl. CK; 14:00 first dressing change with burn nurse. Dietitian, PT/OT and case management consults pending.

notes.title: Pharmacy Admission Note
notes.author: A. Chen, PharmD
notes.summary: Pharmacy admission review: med rec, Parkland and drug dosing checks, sedation, prophylaxis and burn-specific monitoring.
notes.body:
**Patient**
34 M, 82 kg (dosing weight), 180 cm, IBW 75 kg, 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, intubated. NKDA. Cr 0.9 (02:40, 06:00). Vitals at 07:00: HR 111, BP 99/57 (MAP 71), temp 98.2 F, UOP 33 mL/h (last hour).

**Medication Reconciliation**
Sources: partner Jenna Whitaker and chart. No home prescription medications. Cetirizine 10 mg PO PRN for seasonal allergies (hold while NPO). No herbals or supplements reported. No known allergies. Tobacco 1 ppd: nicotine withdrawal possible; offer patch if agitation or per MD. Alcohol use: thiamine, folate, MVI ordered.

**Parkland Check**
4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR/24 h from 01:30. EMS 500 mL counted. LR 450 mL/h since 02:30; increased to 540 mL/h at 06:00 for UOP 25-26 mL/h x 2 h (goal 30-50 mL/h). Calculation verified; no bag labeling issues. Flag fluid creep risk.

**Sedation and Analgesia**
Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min (about 15 mL/h) provides about 390 kcal/day from lipid; baseline triglycerides needed (check Tuesday 06:00) and monitor for propofol infusion syndrome with prolonged high doses. Fentanyl 100 mcg/h (about 1.2 mcg/kg/h); burn patients often need higher opioid requirements and tolerance develops. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV for dressing changes. Avoid routine benzodiazepines (delirium).

**Stress Ulcer and VTE Prophylaxis**
Pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily (first dose 09:00) appropriate: ventilated, burn over 20% TBSA. Heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h (first dose 06:00); burn patients at high VTE risk. Platelets 288, baseline aPTT 29; monitor platelets at least every 48 h for HIT (also on nebulized heparin 5,000 units q8h; systemic absorption minimal but monitor aPTT).

**Acetaminophen**
1,000 mg IV q8h (3 g/day) scheduled. Max 4 g/day; given alcohol use, burn hypermetabolism and AST/ALT pending, cap at 3 g/day. Check LFTs Tuesday.

**Burn-specific Drug Issues**
- Early (first 48 h): decreased clearance and larger Vd (edema). After 48-72 h: hypermetabolic, increased renal and hepatic clearance, so beta-lactams and aminoglycosides may need higher or more frequent dosing, vancomycin levels more important. Hypoalbuminemia (3.8 now, falling with resuscitation) raises free fraction of highly bound drugs. Avoid IM/subcutaneous routes in burned tissue (erratic absorption); use IV or enteral.
- Rocuronium given 02:50; effect resolved by now (verify train of four if needed).
- Vitamin C 500 mg BID, zinc 220 mg daily and MVI per burn protocol; start with feeds at 09:00.

**Antimicrobial Plan**
No systemic prophylactic antibiotics. Topicals: silver sulfadiazine 1% daily (first application 14:00, monitor WBC for transient leukopenia); bacitracin ointment BID to face. Tdap given 03:30. Monitor for fever, wound changes; pharmacy ready to dose empiric therapy (vancomycin 20 mg/kg load, pip-tazo) if infection suspected.

**Monitoring**
BMP/Mg/Phos q6h, CBC q12h, LFTs/TG Tuesday, glucose, CK x3, COHb, daily weights not applicable while resuscitating. Pharmacy will follow daily.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: Day shift head-to-toe assessment after bedside handoff from E. Haddad, RN; stable on LR 540 mL/h.
notes.body:
**Handoff / safety**
- Bedside handoff from E. Haddad, RN at 07:00 with lines, drips, alarms and restraint checked. ID band verified. Contact precautions. Bed low, HOB 30, suction and BVM at bedside.

**Vitals (07:00)**
- HR 111 ST, BP 99/57 (MAP 71), RR 18, SpO2 99%, T 98.2 °F bladder.

**Systems**
- Neuro: RASS -3 on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils 3 mm equal brisk. CPOT 1/8. No spontaneous following of commands (appropriate for goal).
- Resp: 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth, secure, lip-side skin intact. AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.6; PIP 28/Pplat 21. BS coarse bilaterally, small amount of gray-tinged thin secretions on suctioning. Heparin neb given 07:00.
- CV: sinus tachycardia 111, no ectopy. MAP 71 (goal >=65). Generalized edema, face and chest swelling, expected. L hand warm, cap refill 2 s. R hand: radial and ulnar Doppler signals present, forearm soft, no pallor; arm elevated and splinted.
- GI: OG to low intermittent suction, small green-clear output; abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds hypoactive. NPO pending feeding order.
- GU: Foley patent, urine dark amber turning amber. UOP 06:00-07:00 33 mL (0.40 mL/kg/h) on LR 540 mL/h - improving but still below the 41 mL/h target.
- Skin: R arm and chest dressings dry and intact, minimal serosanguineous strike-through at escharotomy sites. Face: erythema, blistering, no new drainage. Back and heels intact; low air loss mattress.
- Lines: L IJ CVC CHG dressing intact, no erythema; L AC 18 g patent; L radial A-line site clean, art BP matches NIBP.
- Restraint: soft L wrist, circulation, skin and sensation intact.

**Plan**
- Hourly UOP, titrate LR per Dr. Okafor; 08:00 ABG/COHb; turn q2h; Parkland phase change at 09:30; dressing change 14:00.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Parkland Phase 2 / Morning Care
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: LR changed to 225 mL/h at 09:30 (hours 8-24 from injury); UOP trend; pantoprazole, oral care and vitamins given.
notes.body:
**Fluid resuscitation**
- First 8 h of Parkland complete at 09:30 (01:30 injury time): 500 mL EMS + ED/ICU LR, about 3,965 mL given vs 3,608 mL goal. Per Dr. Okafor's order LR rate changed 540 -> 225 mL/h at 09:30 (second half of 7,216 mL goal over hours 8-24, to be titrated hourly to UOP). Rate verified with second RN.
- UOP trend: 06-07 33 mL, 07-08 40 mL, 08-09 44 mL (0.54 mL/kg/h); current hour pending. Urine light amber. Goal 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h = 41). Will notify burn team for UOP <30 mL/h x2 h or >50 mL/h x2 h.

**Vitals (09:00)**
- HR 108 ST, BP 103/60 (MAP 74), RR 17, SpO2 99%, T 98.5 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. PIP 28/Pplat 21 on FiO2 0.6, PEEP 5.

**Labs**
- 08:00 ABG: pH 7.38, PaCO2 40, PaO2 172, HCO3 23, COHb 3.1%, lactate 2.2 (improving). 06:00 BMP: K 4.5, Ca 8.4, Cr 0.9, glucose 156. Troponin 0.02 at 08:50 (second, unchanged).

**Medications / care (09:00)**
- Pantoprazole 40 mg IV (stress ulcer prophylaxis). Chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse 15 mL (VAP bundle). Via OG: vitamin C 500 mg, zinc 220 mg, multivitamin with minerals, thiamine 100 mg and folic acid 1 mg - OG clamped 30 min then returned to LIS. Bacitracin thin layer to face.
- Albuterol neb 08:00 and heparin neb 07:00 per inhalation protocol; acetylcysteine due 11:00.
- Turned and repositioned off R arm and chest, R arm re-elevated on pillows; skin on sacrum/heels intact.

**Neurovascular**
- Hourly R hand checks: Doppler radial/ulnar present, forearm soft, no pallor. L hand A-line site OK.

**Plan**
- Trophic tube feeds planned 10:00. Continue hourly UOP and neurovascular checks; family update by Dr. Okafor at rounds; Jenna at bedside.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Enteral Feeding Initiation
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: Osmolite 1.5 started at 20 mL/h via OG at 10:00; tolerance, HOB 30, glucose 164.
notes.body:
**Feeding start**
- Tube feeding started 10:00 per order: Osmolite 1.5 via 16 Fr OG at 20 mL/h, advance 10 mL/h every 4 h to goal 70 mL/h (next 14:00 to 30 mL/h). Free water flush 30 mL every 4 h.
- Before starting: OG position confirmed (CXR 03:05 placement; mark at lips unchanged), suction disconnected. Initial gastric aspirate 15 mL green-clear, returned. Abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds present but hypoactive x4, no stool since admission.
- HOB maintained >=30 degrees. Tolerating without retching or pulmonary changes. Residuals to be checked q4h: hold feeds and call provider for >500 mL. Feeds are not held for dressing changes (hold only for OR/extubation).

**Glucose**
- POC glucose 164 mg/dL at 10:00 (156 serum at 06:00). Stress hyperglycemia expected; recheck with 12:00 labs; insulin per protocol if persistently >180.

**Vitals (10:00)**
- HR 107 ST, BP 104/61 (MAP 75), RR 17, SpO2 100%, T 98.6 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. PIP 28/Pplat 21, FiO2 0.6, PEEP 5.

**Fluids / UOP**
- LR 225 mL/h plus feeds 20 mL/h. UOP 09-10 43 mL (0.52 mL/kg/h), in goal range. Current hour pending.

**Other**
- Oral care with chlorhexidine done at 09:00; ETT 24 cm at teeth, cuff pressure rechecked, stable. R hand Doppler present, forearm soft.
- Dietitian P. Moreno, RD consult pending; will relay tolerance and residual results.

notes.title: Initial Nutrition Assessment
notes.author: P. Moreno, RD
notes.summary: Initial RD assessment for 22% TBSA burn on ventilator: needs about 2,450 kcal and 1.5-2 g/kg protein, trophic feeds started 10:00, micronutrient plan, refeeding risk.
notes.body:
**Reason for Assessment**
Hypermetabolic 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, intubated, RD consult within 24 h.

**Anthropometrics**
Height 180 cm, weight 82 kg (admission, pre-resuscitation; dosing weight 82 kg), IBW 75 kg (109% IBW), BMI 25.3. Weight now unreliable due to resuscitation edema. No recent weight loss per partner; well nourished before injury.

**Nutrition-relevant History**
No GI history. Alcohol 4-6 beers on weekends (more on the night of injury; ethanol 42 mg/dL), tobacco 1 ppd. Normal diet, independent. NKDA.

**Current Nutrition Support**
NPO, OG tube 16 Fr (CXR confirmed). Osmolite 1.5 started 10:00 at 20 mL/h (trophic), advance 10 mL/h q4h (30 mL/h at 14:00) to goal 70 mL/h, expected around 06:00 Tuesday. Free water flush 30 mL q4h. No GI intolerance; residuals not an issue so far, abdomen soft. HOB 30 degrees. Do not hold feeds for dressing changes.

**Estimated Needs**
- Energy: about 2,450 kcal/day (Toronto-type hypermetabolic estimate, about 30 kcal/kg); Curreri formula (25 kcal/kg + 40 kcal x %TBSA) gives about 2,930 kcal and tends to overestimate, so not used.
- Protein: 1.5-2 g/kg = 123-164 g/day (goal about 130 g). Goal feeds provide 2,520 kcal and 105 g protein; add protein modular (e.g., 4 packets/day, about 24 g) to reach about 130 g.
- Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min supplies about 390 kcal/day from lipid; count it. Will reassess goal rate on Tuesday with propofol dose and prealbumin.
- Fluid per resuscitation protocol.

**Labs (12:00, 18:00 pending)**
Na 136, K 4.9, Cl 105, CO2 22, BUN 17, Cr 1.0, glucose 172, Ca 8.1, Mg 1.9, Phos 3.0. Albumin 3.8 (admission; will fall with resuscitation and is not a nutrition marker). CK 1,120. Lactate 1.8. Triglycerides and prealbumin planned Tuesday.

**Micronutrients**
Ascorbic acid 500 mg BID, zinc sulfate 220 mg daily, multivitamin with minerals daily, thiamine 100 mg and folic acid 1 mg daily started 09:00. Monitor Cu/Se levels later in stay.

**Refeeding Risk**
Moderate: alcohol use, burn stress. Thiamine given before feeds. Monitor K, Mg, Phos q6h (Phos 3.0 now); replete before advancing if Phos under 2.5. Advance feeds per schedule.

**Glycemic**
Glucose 164-181, goal 140-180. Insulin infusion if persistently over 180 per ICU.

**Plan**
1. Continue advance to goal 70 mL/h. 2. Protein modular at goal. 3. Daily RD follow-up; nitrogen balance when able. 4. Weekly weights when edema resolves. 5. Transition to oral supplements after extubation and swallow screen.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Midday UOP Trend, Rate Change and Family Update
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: Downtrending UOP prompted call to Dr. Okafor; LR increased 225 to 270 mL/h at 14:00; family update and restraint checks.
notes.body:
**Fluid titration**
- UOP trend: 10-11 36 mL, 11-12 32 mL, 12-13 28 mL (0.34 mL/kg/h), 13-14 28 mL (0.34 mL/kg/h). Steady decline from 43 mL/h (10:00) and below the 41 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h) target on LR 225 mL/h with MAP 76-78, urine amber.
- SBAR to Dr. Okafor by phone at 13:05: UOP below goal and downtrending; B: Parkland hour 12, 22% TBSA; A: HR 103, MAP 76, lactate 1.8 and CK 1,120 at 12:00, no myoglobinuria, PIP 27/Pplat 20, R hand Doppler intact; R: increase rate. Order: LR 225 -> 270 mL/h at 14:00 (20% increase); read back and rate changed with second-RN verification at 14:00. Feeds advanced to 30 mL/h at 14:00 per protocol. Recheck UOP hourly.

**Vitals (13:00 / 14:00)**
- HR 103 -> 102 ST, BP 105/61 (MAP 76) -> 108/63 (MAP 78), RR 17-18, SpO2 99%, T 99.0 °F. RASS -3. CPOT 1/8 at 13:00, 4/8 at 14:00 during dressing preparation; hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 13:45 (see dressing note). FiO2 0.5 at 14:00 per RT after 12:00 ABG (7.39/39/134, COHb 3.0%).

**Family**
- Mother Linda Delaney arrived ~11:30, tearful on first sight of patient. Jenna Whitaker and Linda at bedside. Explained ventilator, sedation, why he is asleep, hourly urine checks and fluids, wound dressings, contact precautions (gown/glove), and the plan for dressing change at 14:00. Both asked appropriate questions and verbalized understanding. Encouraged touching unburned left hand and talking to him. They stepped out for the dressing change.

**Safety**
- Soft L wrist restraint: circulation, skin, sensation checked q2h (last 14:00), skin intact, cap refill 2 s; restraint order current. ETT 24 cm at teeth. R arm elevated, hand Doppler present hourly. HOB 30.

**Plan**
- Reassess UOP at 15:00 and hourly; call burn team if <30 mL/h x2 more hours or <20 mL/h x1.

notes.title: Burn Wound Assessment and Dressing Change
notes.author: N. Ibarra, RN
notes.summary: First 14:00 dressing change: wounds by area, no signs of infection, silver sulfadiazine applied, pain premedicated.
notes.body:
**Reason**
Daily burn wound assessment and dressing change at 14:00 with J. Morales, RN. 22% TBSA flame burn. Sterile technique, gown, gloves, mask.

**Pain Management**
Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given 13:45. CPOT 4/8 at 14:00 during removal of dressings (grimace, tense muscle tone), 1/8 by 15:00. Continuous fentanyl 100 mcg/h and propofol 30 mcg/kg/min running. RASS -3.

**Vitals**
14:00 HR 102, BP 108/63 (MAP 78), RR 18, SpO2 99%, temp 99.0 F. 15:00 HR 102, BP 107/62 (MAP 77).

**Wound Description by Area**
- Right forearm and hand (circumferential, 3rd degree): leathery, waxy white to tan, dry, nonblanching, insensate to pinprick; escharotomy incisions mid-medial and mid-lateral from forearm across wrist and hand, edges gaping, clean red-pink fat, scant serosanguinous ooze, no active bleeding. Fingers edematous, pink at tips, cap refill 2 sec, Doppler signals radial/ulnar and digital present.
- Right upper arm (deep partial): mottled red and white, ruptured blisters, moist, slow cap refill, no odor.
- Anterior chest (deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches): pale/white-tan areas about 3 cm each, surrounding deep red moist tissue. Drainage scant to moderate serosanguinous.
- Face and neck: superficial-partial, erythema, intact and ruptured blisters on cheeks and forehead, brows singed, lips edematous, no eschar.
- No purulence, no foul odor, no surrounding spreading erythema.

**Care Provided**
Dressings soaked off with saline; wounds cleansed with mild soap and sterile water, loose blisters debrided per protocol. Silver sulfadiazine 1% applied about 1/16 inch thick to the right arm and chest. Covered with non-adherent layer, gauze and loose wrap, fingers wrapped separately with tips visible. Bacitracin to face. Photos taken in the chart media (measurements recorded). Total time about 40 minutes.

**Positioning / Splint**
Right hand splinted in position of function, arm elevated above heart on pillows. Turn side to side without lying on the right arm or chest.

**Response**
Tolerated with transient HR rise. No bleeding. Dressing intact.

**Plan**
Daily change at 14:00 with premedication 15 min before. Hourly neurovascular checks. Watch for fever, odor, purulence, spreading erythema (mark margins), eschar separation. Burn nurse specialist to follow daily. Jenna Whitaker updated.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Burn Dressing Change
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: First daily dressing change with N. Ibarra, RN at 14:00 after hydromorphone 0.5 mg; SSD to chest/R arm, bacitracin to face; tolerated.
notes.body:
**Pre-procedure**
- Daily dressing change at 14:00 with burn nurse N. Ibarra, RN. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 13:45 (15 min premed). Acetaminophen 1,000 mg IV given 14:00. CPOT 1/8 before premed, 4/8 at 14:00 at start of wound manipulation. HR 102, BP 108/63 (MAP 78), SpO2 99%. Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h continued. Gown, gloves, mask, sterile technique; tube feeds continued.

**Procedure**
- Old dressings removed with saline soaks; wounds cleansed and gently debrided of loose tissue. N. Ibarra measured and photographed.
- R forearm/hand: full-thickness, leathery and waxy, escharotomy incisions clean with pink granular edges, minimal ooze. R upper arm: deep partial, moist, mottled. Anterior chest: deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches, no purulence, no odor, no erythema beyond burn margins. Face/neck: superficial to superficial partial, no drainage.
- Silver sulfadiazine 1% cream 1/16 inch applied to chest and R arm and covered with non-adherent gauze and loose wrap. Bacitracin thin layer to face after gentle cleansing.
- R hand splint reapplied in position of function (fingers MCP flexed ~70 degrees, IP extended, thumb abducted); R arm elevated on pillows above heart. Doppler radial/ulnar signals present after wrap, forearm soft, no pallor, wrap not constrictive.

**Tolerance / response**
- Procedure about 40 minutes. Transient HR rise to 108, MAP unchanged; no desaturation. CPOT 3/8 near end, CPOT 1/8 by 15:00. Propofol/fentanyl unchanged. No bleeding.

**Fluids**
- LR 270 mL/h since 14:00; UOP 14-15 37 mL (0.45 mL/kg/h), improving.

**Plan**
- Next dressing change daily 14:00. Monitor for odor, drainage, spreading erythema, eschar changes and fever. Burn nurse to follow splint adjustments with OT.

notes.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
notes.author: S. Kim, PT
notes.summary: PT evaluation: intubated and sedated, passive ROM program, positioning to prevent contractures, baseline fully independent.
notes.body:
**Reason for Referral**
Burn rehabilitation, 22% TBSA right arm and chest burns, ventilated, ICU day 1.

**Prior Level of Function**
Independent in all mobility and ADLs, working full time as an HVAC technician (ladders, crawl spaces, lifting 50-75 lb), right-hand dominant. Lived in a single-story house with partner and daughter. Source: partner.

**Current Status**
Intubated, sedated (RASS -3), unable to participate. Vitals 15:00: HR 102, BP 107/62 (MAP 77), SpO2 99% on FiO2 0.50. Lines: ETT, left IJ CVC, left radial A-line, OG, Foley. Right forearm escharotomy dressings, hand splinted, arm elevated. Strength and sensation unable to test; moves left arm and legs to stimulation.

**Contraindications / Precautions**
- No active exercise while sedated. No stretching across fresh escharotomy incisions or wrist/hand without burn team clearance. Avoid pressure on chest wall and right arm. Hold ROM if MAP under 65, HR over 130, or new arrhythmia. Maintain ETT and line safety, heel offloading. No OOB during resuscitation.

**Plan / Interventions**
- Passive ROM, 10 reps BID, with RN present: left upper extremity and both lower extremities all planes; right shoulder (flexion/abduction to 90 degrees), right elbow to full extension within tolerance. Coordinate premedication with dressing changes.
- Positioning: shoulders abducted about 90 degrees, elbow extended, neck neutral with no pillow behind head if neck contracture risk, ankles neutral with foot positioners to prevent plantarflexion contracture, knees extended.
- Pulmonary support with RT; early mobility progression once resuscitation done: sitting at bedside, then chair.

**Goals**
Short term (1 week): maintain full passive ROM, no contractures, tolerate dangle. Long term: independent household ambulation and return to work with right hand function.

**Frequency**
Daily 5x/week. Discussed positioning with RN. Jenna Whitaker informed of therapy plan.

notes.title: Occupational Therapy Initial Evaluation
notes.author: H. Larsen, OTR/L
notes.summary: OT evaluation: right hand splint in position of function, edema control and elevation, ADL baseline independent.
notes.body:
**Reason for Referral**
Right hand and forearm full-thickness burn s/p escharotomy; splinting, edema and ADL planning.

**Prior Level of Function**
Right-hand dominant, independent in ADLs, IADLs and work as an HVAC technician. Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker and daughter Ava (6).

**Current Status**
Intubated and sedated (RASS -3), HR 102, BP 107/62 (MAP 77). Right hand: marked edema, dressings in place, fingers pink, cap refill about 2 sec, Doppler signals present; cannot assess active movement or sensation. Left hand intact, A-line left wrist.

**Splinting**
Pre-fabricated resting splint applied overnight reviewed and remolded: right volar resting hand splint in the position of safe function: wrist neutral to slight extension (about 20 degrees), MCP joints 60-70 degrees flexion, IP joints extended, thumb abducted with web space open. Padding over wrist incisions, straps loose to avoid pressure, fingertips visible. Skin checked under straps at each dressing change; splint on at all times except dressing changes and therapy.

**Edema Management**
Hand and arm elevated above heart level on pillows/foam wedge; fingertips visible for hourly checks. No compression until burn team approves. Gentle active range when awake.

**ADL / Cognitive Baseline**
Independent in self-care. No cognitive concerns prior to injury; ETOH use noted. Will reassess after extubation.

**Goals**
Maintain MCP flexion and web space, prevent claw hand, minimize edema; independent feeding and grooming with adaptive equipment and left hand within 2 weeks of grafting.

**Plan**
OT daily with PT; splint adjustment as edema changes; nursing to maintain elevation and splint position; teaching to Jenna.

notes.title: Case Management Initial Assessment
notes.author: T. Whitfield, RN CM
notes.summary: CM assessment: commercial insurance through employer, home destroyed, partner as proxy, anticipated 3-4 week stay, rehab and burn clinic planning.
notes.body:
**Reason**
Initial assessment for admission 11/2, 22% TBSA burn with inhalation injury, ICU.

**Insurance / Financial**
Employer-sponsored commercial PPO through the HVAC company; verification started with benefits office. Burn center in network; admission notification and concurrent review in progress. Not a workers' compensation case. Partner reports household income is primarily the patient's. Social work to assist with financial resources.

**Home Situation**
Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker and daughter Ava (6); house destroyed in the fire. Family currently staying with Jenna's mother. Red Cross/fire relief contact to be arranged by social work. Mother Linda Delaney arrived this afternoon.

**Decision-making**
Patient sedated. Full code. Jenna Whitaker at bedside, discussed as health care proxy; advance directive none.

**Anticipated Course**
ICU several days, excision and grafting planned this week. Expected total length of stay about 3-4 weeks (roughly 1 day per % TBSA) depending on grafting and wound healing.

**Discharge Planning Thoughts**
- Likely disposition: home with partner with home health versus acute rehab if hand function and mobility deficits remain. Needs a safe housing plan since the home was lost.
- Outpatient burn clinic follow-up, OT/PT for hand therapy, scar management, pressure garments, wound supplies and DME.
- Return to work: physical HVAC job requiring right-hand function; FMLA and short-term disability paperwork; employer contacted with family permission.
- Barriers: housing, transport, smoking cessation, alcohol counseling.

**Plan**
Follow daily; update team at interdisciplinary rounds; start FMLA paperwork; reassess once off ventilator.

notes.title: Social Work and Chaplain Note
notes.author: K. Abara, LCSW
notes.summary: SW met partner Jenna Whitaker and mother Linda Delaney; daughter Ava safe with grandmother; guilt and distress, supports and ASAP counseling referral placed.
notes.body:
**Reason**
Family support and psychosocial assessment, burn ICU day 1.

**Family**
Partner Jenna Whitaker at bedside; mother Linda Delaney arrived this afternoon. Daughter Ava, 6, uninjured, was checked in the ED and is staying with her maternal grandmother (Jenna's mother). No other children.

**Assessment**
- Jenna is tearful, anxious and sleep deprived, repeatedly saying she is relieved Ava is safe but frightened for Marcus. Expresses guilt that she did not wake him sooner and thoughts about what happened. She understands he is on a ventilator and has burns to the arm and chest. Ava has asked if her father is going to be okay and wants to see him; Jenna is unsure whether it is appropriate.
- Linda is supportive, coping with shock; will stay locally.
- Anticipate Marcus will have guilt and distress when awake given the circumstances.
- Substance use: alcohol use noted; no concerning pattern reported by partner, will screen after extubation.

**Child Safety**
Ava safe with grandmother, calm per Jenna; no concerns for her care identified, no child protective report indicated. Child life referral for preparation before a visit (burns, tubes and monitors).

**Supports / Resources**
Chaplain visit offered; Jenna accepted prayer support today. Provided waiting room, parking and meal vouchers. Red Cross assistance and fire relief resources shared (house lost). Burn survivor peer support information given.

**Referrals**
ASAP (Acute Stress and Adjustment Program) counseling referral placed for Jenna and Ava, and for Marcus once extubated.

**Plan**
SW follows daily during ICU stay, will attend family meeting with Dr. Okafor, assist with housing and financial applications with case management (T. Whitfield).

notes.title: Nursing Note - Afternoon Update (Labs, UOP, Vent, Consults)
notes.author: J. Morales, RN

Hgb 13.6 (17.2 on arrival, hemodilution with resuscitation), plt 246, WBC 16.1. ABG 16:00 pH 7.40, PaCO2 38, PaO2 128, HCO3 24. COHb 3.0% at 12:00.

**Vent**
- AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.5 since 14:00. PIP 27/Pplat 20. Secretions thin white-gray. ETT 24 cm at teeth. Oral care with chlorhexidine due 21:00; HOB 30.

**Glucose**
- POC 164 (10:00), serum 172 (12:00), POC 181 (16:00) - trending up with stress response and feeds; serum due 18:00. Provider aware; insulin infusion per protocol if persistently >180.

**Visits**

Moreno, RD: nutrition assessment, tube feed advance plan to 70 mL/h confirmed. T. Whitfield, RN CM met Jenna and Linda about insurance and support; K. Abara, LCSW offered support resources.

**Pain / neuro / wounds**

notes.title: Critical Care Progress Note, ICU Day 1
notes.author: L. Brandt, MD
notes.summary: ICU day 1 course: resuscitation on track with UOP in range, COHb cleared, FiO2 weaned to 0.50, plan overnight.
notes.body:
**Subjective / Interval Events**
Patient intubated and sedated, RASS -3. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg given 13:45 for the 14:00 dressing change (CPOT 4, back to 1). Partner Jenna Whitaker and mother Linda Delaney at bedside, updated. No acute events.

**Objective (18:00)**

notes.body:
**Event**

**Interventions**
- Stayed at bedside, reoriented verbally, reassured. Checked for causes: ETT 24 cm at teeth confirmed, cuff pressure 24 cmH2O, suctioned thin secretions, no kinking; ventilator asynchrony reviewed with RT. Soft L wrist restraint retained (checked: circulation, skin intact, order current); placed bite block. Pain assessed CPOT 1-2/8, no dressing/pain trigger. Hydromorphone not needed.
- Dr. Brandt (on-call intensivist) notified at 02:55 by phone (SBAR). Order: lorazepam 1 mg IV x1. Given 03:00; propofol held at 35 for now with plan to decrease to 30 at 04:00 once calm (Tuesday RASS goal -1 to -2).

**Response**
- By 03:15 RASS -3, calm, synchronous with vent, no biting. HR 93, BP 109/64 (MAP 79), RR 16, SpO2 98% at 03:00. PIP 24/Pplat 17. ETT remains 24 cm, no airway injury; lips and teeth intact, no bleeding. No unplanned extubation.

**Glucose / insulin**

**Notifications / plan**
- Charge RN B. Sutton informed. Family not present; will update Jenna at morning call. Hourly RASS/CPOT; watch for delirium (lorazepam is a delirium risk - use sparingly). Discuss SAT/sedation plan with day team at 08:00.

notes.title: Respiratory Therapy Daily Note - Ventilator Day 2
notes.author: D. Alvarez, RRT
notes.summary: Ventilator day 2 on AC/VC FiO2 0.40/PEEP 5, SAT done at 08:00, not yet ready for SBT during resuscitation; VAP bundle and inhalation-injury nebulizer protocol continued.
notes.body:
**Reason for Note**
Daily ventilator management, ICU day 2. Flame burn 22% TBSA with grade 2 inhalation injury (bronchoscopy 04:20 Mon). Intubated 02:50 Mon in the ED.

**Events / Subjective**
- SAT performed 08:00 with J. Morales, RN: propofol held (was 30 mcg/kg/min), fentanyl continued at 100 mcg/h. Patient woke to voice, followed commands with the left hand, was tearful, coughed forcefully on the ETT. No ventilator dyssynchrony or biting. During SAT HR 92, BP 110/65 (MAP 80), RR 17, SpO2 98%.
- Propofol restarted 08:35 at 20 mcg/kg/min for tearfulness and ongoing resuscitation per burn team.
- Current RASS -2, CPOT 1/8.

**Ventilator Settings (08:00)**
- Mode AC/VC, VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW 75 kg), set RR 16, total RR 17, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40 (weaned from 0.50 at 04:00).
- PIP 24, Pplat 17 cmH2O, driving pressure 12, static compliance about 38 mL/cmH2O.
- ETT 8.0 oral, 24 cm at the teeth, cuff pressure 24 cmH2O (goal 20-30), re-checked this shift. Ties and bite block intact, no skin breakdown at the lips.

**ABG (06:00, FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5)**
pH 7.41 / PaCO2 40 / PaO2 124 / HCO3 25 / BE +1, SaO2 98%, lactate 1.4. P/F ratio 310. Last COHb 3.0% (Mon 12:00), resolved. Pulse oximetry now reliable.

**Secretions / Breath Sounds**
Moderate thin white-tan secretions via in-line suction, suctioned 3 times since 04:00. Carbonaceous flecks markedly less than Monday. Breath sounds coarse bilaterally with scattered rhonchi that clear with suctioning; no wheeze. No bronchoscopy needed today.

**Nebulized Inhalation Injury Protocol**
Albuterol 2.5 mg q4h (last 08:00), acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL q8h (last 03:00, next 11:00), heparin 5,000 units nebulized q8h (last 07:00). Given in-line, albuterol first, then acetylcysteine, then heparin, with suction after. No bronchospasm, no tachycardia response. Continue per protocol.

**Weaning Assessment**
Not ready for SBT today. Reasons: still in the resuscitation phase (Parkland window ended 01:30; albumin 5% 500 mL running 06:00-10:00 with LR 75 mL/h), airway and facial edema with fluid shifts, FiO2 0.50-0.40 with PEEP 5 only since Monday afternoon, 14:00 dressing change requires sedation, no cuff leak test yet. Plan to reassess for SAT/SBT pairing Wednesday morning.

**VAP Bundle**
- HOB 30-35 degrees confirmed; oral care with chlorhexidine 0.12% q12h (next 09:00) plus oral suction q4h and PRN
- Daily SAT done; SBT screen done (fails readiness)
- Pantoprazole and SQ heparin on MAR
- Closed in-line suction, circuit not changed unless soiled; subglottic suction ETT not available
- Cuff pressure checks q shift

**Plan**
1. Continue AC/VC 450 x 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40, titrate FiO2 for SpO2 92% or higher.
2. Continue nebulizer protocol; suction PRN.
3. ABG with next scheduled draw and with any ventilator or clinical change.
4. Daily CXR 05:00 reviewed with team.
5. Will reassess SBT candidacy tomorrow 08:00 with RN, MD.

D. Alvarez, RRT, Respiratory Therapy, filed 08:45.

- Mouthed "mom" and became tearful. Mother Linda Delaney was at bedside and spoke to him; he calmed and held her hand. Reoriented to place and reason for ICU stay by nodding to simple questions.
- CPOT 1-2/8 during the interruption (mild grimace with repositioning only); no hydromorphone needed.

- Pulled gently against the left wrist restraint once; redirected, restraint maintained for ETT/line protection, circulation intact.
- CAM-ICU negative (RASS 0, attentive, follows commands, no disorganized thinking).

**Restart**
Propofol restarted at 08:35 at 20 mcg/kg/min (half the prior 30). RASS settled at -1 to -2. Plan to increase to 30 mcg/kg/min at 09:30 if RASS stays within the -1 to -2 goal and comfort allows; titrate by RASS and CPOT.

**SBT**
No spontaneous breathing trial today. Patient is still in the active post-resuscitation fluid-shift phase with albumin 5% infusing until 10:00, FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, and burn team/intensivist plan is to reassess for extubation tomorrow after the dressing and sepsis surveillance; discussed with RT D. Alvarez, RRT.

**Family**

**Plan**
Continue hourly RASS/CPOT, CAM-ICU each shift, oral care, HOB above 30 degrees, left-hand neuro checks, pre-medicate for the 14:00 dressing change.

notes.title: Nutrition Follow-Up Note
notes.author: P. Moreno, RD
notes.summary: Tube feeds at goal 70 mL/h since 06:00; low prealbumin and phosphorus 2.1 (refeeding/burn losses); propofol calories counted; recommends protein modular and electrolyte repletion.
notes.body:
**Reason for Follow-Up**
Hypermetabolic burn patient (22% TBSA, about 8% full-thickness, inhalation injury), mechanically ventilated, enteral nutrition day 2. Admission weight 82 kg, height 180 cm, IBW 75 kg. Bed-scale weight not reliable with edema and arm elevation.

**Nutrition Support**
- Osmolite 1.5 via OG tube started Mon 10:00 at 20 mL/h, advanced by 10 mL/h q4h, reached goal 70 mL/h at 06:00 today. Tolerating: abdomen soft, no emesis, gastric residuals below 100 mL per RN, no loose stool. Bladder pressures 10-14 mmHg during resuscitation.
- Goal regimen delivers about 1,680 mL/day = 2,520 kcal and 105 g protein, plus free water flushes 30 mL q4h.
- Estimated needs: about 2,450 kcal/day (Toronto-type estimate; Curreri about 2,930 and likely overestimates), protein 1.5-2 g/kg = 125-165 g/day. Indirect calorimetry not available.
- Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min (14.8 mL/h of 10 mg/mL) provides about 390 kcal/day from lipid, so total delivered is about 2,900 kcal/day. Slightly above estimated needs, accepted while sedated; will reduce EN if propofol continues at higher rates or if glucose/triglycerides rise.

**Pertinent Labs**
- Prealbumin 7.1 mg/dL (low; acute-phase suppressed, trend only), albumin 2.6 g/dL
- Triglycerides 168 mg/dL at 06:00 on propofol (mildly high, acceptable; recheck Thursday)
- Phosphorus 2.1 mg/dL (3.4 on admission), Mg 1.6 mg/dL (low), K 3.9, Na 134, Ca 7.7, BUN 23, creatinine 1.1
- Glucose 177 at 06:00; POC glucose 169-179 mg/dL this morning on insulin infusion 1.5 units/h (started 00:30). Latest 173 at 10:30.
- AST 72, ALT 58 (mild, stress/burn related)

**Assessment**
Severe burn hypermetabolism with early protein-calorie deficit risk. Falling phosphorus and magnesium after feeding advancement and fluid shifts indicate refeeding physiology plus burn and resuscitation losses. High risk for hyperglycemia from stress response and overfeeding. Protein delivery of 105 g is below the 1.5-2 g/kg range needed for wound healing.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue Osmolite 1.5 at 70 mL/h; do NOT hold for dressing changes (hold only for OR or extubation).
2. Add protein modular 15 g BID via OG (30 g/day) to reach about 135 g protein/day.
3. Replete phosphorus, magnesium and potassium per MD protocol; recheck BMP/Mg/Phos q6h until phosphorus is 2.5 or higher.
4. Continue thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, multivitamin with minerals, vitamin C 500 mg BID, zinc sulfate 220 mg daily (wound healing).
5. Continue insulin infusion for goal glucose 140-180 mg/dL; reassess EN total if insulin requirement climbs.
6. Calorie and protein adjustment needed when propofol is weaned: EN becomes the sole source.
7. Weekly weights when feasible; prealbumin and CRP weekly; consider 24-hour urine urea nitrogen Thursday.

P. Moreno, RD, will follow daily.

notes.title: Wound Care Specialist Note - New Concerning Findings
notes.author: N. Ibarra, RN (Burn Nurse Specialist)
notes.summary: At the 14:00 dressing change the right chest and arm wounds showed new purulent drainage, foul odor, spreading erythema and a dark violaceous area at the right chest border; margin marked and burn surgeon notified.
notes.body:
**Reason for Visit**
Daily burn dressing change at 14:00 with J. Morales, RN. Premedicated with hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV at 13:45. Gown, gloves, mask, sterile technique.

**Pre-Procedure Status**
HR 105, BP 106/55 (MAP 72), RR 20, SpO2 98% on vent (FiO2 0.40), Tbladder 100.4 F (99.9 F at 13:00, 99.5 F at 09:00). CPOT rose to 5/8 with dressing removal (1/8 at rest), propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. UOP 41 mL/h at 13:00-14:00.

**Findings**
- Right anterior chest (deep partial with full-thickness patches): new thick yellow-green purulent drainage on the inner dressings, foul odor noted on removal (was none Monday). Eschar beginning to separate at the lateral/inferior border, with a dark violaceous, non-blanching area about 4 x 5 cm at the right chest border and loss of the adjacent eschar adherence.
- Erythema spreading beyond the burn margin, about 2-3 cm in the lateral chest wall and toward the axilla, warm, indurated. Margin traced with skin marker at 14:30 and dated/timed on the skin.
- Right upper arm (deep partial): moist, increased exudate, no frank pus; forearm and hand (full-thickness) with escharotomy incisions open, clean, no purulence. Doppler signals present at radial and ulnar arteries of the right hand, capillary refill sluggish but present at fingertips, no tense compartments.
- Face/neck: superficial areas clean, dry, bacitracin applied, no concern.
- Pain response increased on chest assessment (grimacing, guarding), CPOT 5.

**Care Provided**
Wound cleansed with warm saline and chlorhexidine-free wound cleanser, loose debris removed, no sharp debridement performed. Photographs (6) taken with measurement ruler and uploaded to the media tab. Silver sulfadiazine 1% reapplied per the current order pending surgeon review, covered with dry sterile dressings, arm elevated and splint reapplied. Patient tolerated with transient HR rise to 108 and CPOT back to 4 by 15:00.

**Culture Plan**
Wound swab from the area of purulent drainage after cleansing, plus recommend blood cultures x2, tracheal aspirate, urine culture and lactate/procalcitonin (sepsis order set) given fever trend, tachycardia and fall in UOP. Cultures to be drawn before any antimicrobial. Biopsy for quantitative culture and histology per surgeon.

**Notifications**
- J. Morales, RN notified at bedside and agrees to escalate on SBAR.
- Dr. Okafor (Burn Surgery) paged 14:40, returned call 14:45; will examine at the bedside this afternoon and decide on topical agent change and biopsy. Will update Dr. Brandt.

**Recommendations**
1. Surgeon bedside exam today; consider switch to mafenide acetate (eschar penetration).
2. Monitor temperature, HR, MAP, UOP and glucose q1h; watch for sepsis.
3. Recheck the marked margin q4h and with each shift, document change in mm.
4. Maintain contact precautions and dedicated equipment.

N. Ibarra, RN, Burn Nurse Specialist, will return for the next dressing change.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Sepsis SBAR
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: SBAR notification of surgeon and intensivist for fever, tachycardia and falling urine output with infected wound.
notes.body:
**S (Situation)**
Suspected burn wound sepsis. At 15:30 T 101.1 F, HR 113, BP 105/51 (MAP 69), RR 23, SpO2 96% on the ventilator. Called Dr. Okafor (burn surgery) and Dr. Brandt (critical care) at 15:40.

**B (Background)**
34 y/o male, 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, hospital day 2, intubated. Wound change at 14:00 dressing change with N. Ibarra: new purulent drainage, foul odor, spreading erythema beyond the burn margin, eschar separation with dark violaceous area at the right chest border. NKDA, Full Code.

**A (Assessment)**
- Trend: T 99.9 (13:00), 100.4 (14:00), 100.9 (15:00), 101.1 (15:30). HR 97, 105, 108, 113. MAP 77, 72, 71, 69. RR 18 to 23.
- UOP falling: 45 (1200-1300), 41 (1300-1400), 36 mL (1400-1500) = 0.44 mL/kg/h and trending down.
- POC glucose 205 at 15:30 (was 173 this morning); insulin infusion raised to 1.5 units/h at 15:00.
- Pain CPOT 4/8; RASS -2. Skin warm, fingertips with brisk cap refill. Last WBC 15.4, lactate 1.4 (06:00), K 3.6.
I am concerned this is early sepsis from the wound infection.

**R (Recommendation / orders received)**
Dr. Okafor and Dr. Brandt acknowledged and gave orders:
- Cultures x4 sites before antibiotics: wound swab from area of drainage, blood x2 (peripheral and central line), tracheal aspirate, urine from Foley.
- Lactate, procalcitonin, CBC with differential, coags.
- Broad-spectrum antibiotics after cultures; pharmacy to dose.
- Dr. Okafor to examine the wound at the bedside; further orders to follow.

**Actions**
Cultures being collected at 15:50 with sterile technique. Antibiotic orders being verified with A. Chen, PharmD. Hourly vitals, strict I&O, and Foley output continue. Sepsis screen documented. Mother Linda informed that a fever and a possible infection are being treated.

**Plan**
Draw lactate/PCT/CBC immediately after cultures, give antibiotics within 1 hour, track MAP goal 65 or higher and UOP 0.5 mL/kg/h, call for MAP under 65, UOP under 30 mL/h, or any worsening.

notes.title: Burn Surgery Event Note - Early Invasive Burn Wound Infection
notes.author: R. Okafor, MD
notes.summary: Bedside wound exam 16:30 consistent with early invasive burn wound infection; biopsy sent, silver sulfadiazine stopped, mafenide soaks starting 17:30, broad antibiotics given.
notes.body:
**Reason for Note**
Event note: concern for burn wound infection raised by N. Ibarra, RN at 14:00 dressing change, and by RN SBAR at 15:30 for fever, tachycardia and falling urine output.

**Interval History**
Post-burn day 2. Resuscitation phase complete (Parkland 24 h ended 01:30). Since about 13:00 temperature has risen from 99.9 F to 101.4 F (16:30), HR 97 to 116, RR 26, MAP 67. UOP 28 mL/h at 15:00-16:00 (0.34 mL/kg/h) on LR 100 mL/h. CPOT 5 with dressing change, now 2.

**Exam (bedside 16:30)**
- Vitals 16:30: HR 116, BP 105/48 (67), RR 26, SpO2 96%, T 101.4 F. Ventilated, RASS -2.
- Right anterior chest: purulent drainage and foul odor, eschar separating along the lateral/inferior border with a dark violaceous area about 4 x 5 cm, surrounding erythema 2-3 cm beyond the burn margin, at the 14:30 marker line and extending slightly past it superolaterally. Tissue under separating eschar is soft, dusky, no bleeding on probing.
- Right upper arm deep partial: increased exudate, no purulence. Right forearm and hand full thickness: escharotomy sites clean, Doppler signals intact.
- Face and neck: no change.

**Data**
Lactate 2.9, WBC 18.4 (12.8 on admission, 15.4 at noon), Hgb 11.6, platelets 171, INR 1.4, aPTT 38, procalcitonin 4.8 (15:55). Creatinine 1.1 at noon. Cultures sent 15:50: blood x2 (peripheral and central), wound, tracheal aspirate, urine.

**Procedure**
Punch biopsy of the wound-margin tissue from the right chest border (viable/nonviable interface) obtained 16:35 after local lidocaine with existing sedation/analgesia; hemostasis with pressure. Specimens to microbiology for quantitative culture and to pathology for histology (looking for organism invasion of viable tissue). No complications.

**Assessment**
Early invasive burn wound infection of the right chest (and possibly arm) with systemic inflammatory response, likely evolving burn wound sepsis. Gram-positive organism (S. aureus) most likely at day 2, but Gram-negatives including Pseudomonas must be covered until cultures return. Evidence of hypoperfusion (lactate rising, oliguria).

**Plan**
1. Stop silver sulfadiazine (discontinued 16:45). Start mafenide acetate 5% solution soaks to right chest and right arm at 17:30, then q8h; keep gauze moist. Monitor for metabolic acidosis (BMP, ABG) and pain with application; premedicate.
2. Antibiotics: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV extended infusion started 16:30; vancomycin load 1,750 mg started 16:45; pharmacy dosing. Narrow when cultures and biopsy return.
3. Sepsis bundle with Dr. Brandt: fluid bolus, repeat lactate, vasopressor if MAP under 65; ICU team managing.
4. Re-mark erythema margin q4h; photos daily.
5. Early excision and autografting of right chest, forearm and hand once hemodynamically stable and infection controlled; tentatively Friday 11-06; will discuss consent with family. Type and screen current.
6. Continue hourly neurovascular checks right hand, elevation, splint.
7. Will re-examine in the morning and sooner for hemodynamic change.

R. Okafor, MD, Burn Surgery, filed 16:45.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Sepsis Bundle Progress
notes.author: J. Morales, RN
notes.summary: Cultures and sepsis labs done, antibiotics started, surgeon exam completed.
notes.body:
**Cultures (collected 15:50, before antibiotics)**

- Blood culture set 2: left IJ central line.
- Wound swab: right chest/arm at area of drainage after cleansing.

**Antibiotics**
- Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV extended infusion (4 h) started 16:30.
- Vancomycin load 1,750 mg IV over 2 h started 16:45 via a separate lumen of the left IJ. The two drugs run on separate lumens; no co-infusion. Pharmacy (A. Chen, PharmD) verified doses (20 mg/kg load).

**Wound exam**
Dr. Okafor examined the burn wound at 16:30 with N. Ibarra, RN present and took a biopsy. Silver sulfadiazine discontinued. Mafenide acetate 5% soaks ordered, to start with the next wound care (q8h); anticipate increased pain with mafenide, so pre-medicate. OR for excision/grafting planned once he is stable.

**Hemodynamics**
16:00: T 101.2 F, HR 115, BP 104/51 (MAP 69), RR 25, SpO2 97%. 16:30: T 101.4 F, HR 116, BP 105/48 (MAP 67), RR 26, SpO2 96%. UOP 28 mL for the 1500-1600 hour (0.34 mL/kg/h). Propofol 30, fentanyl 100 mcg/h, CPOT 2/8, RASS -2. FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5, PIP 26 / Pplat 19. Feeds continue at 70 mL/h.

**Notified**

notes.title: Nursing Note - Hypotension and Vasopressor Start

notes.title: Critical Care Event Note - Sepsis / Septic Shock
notes.author: L. Brandt, MD
notes.summary: Burn wound sepsis progressing to vasopressor-requiring shock; cultures sent, pip-tazo and vancomycin given, two LR boluses, norepinephrine started 17:30; ventilator and steroid plans.
notes.body:
**Reason for Note**
Event note, sepsis / septic shock in setting of early invasive right chest/arm burn wound infection, called by RN and burn team.

**Timeline Since 13:00**
- 13:00: T 99.9 F, HR 97, MAP 77, UOP 45 mL/h
- 14:00: T 100.4 F, HR 105, MAP 72; wound change shows purulence (see Wound Care and Burn Surgery notes)
- 15:30: T 101.1 F, HR 113, RR 23, MAP 69; RN SBAR to Dr. Okafor and me
- 15:50-15:55: cultures (blood x2, wound, tracheal aspirate, urine) and labs: lactate 2.9, WBC 18.4, platelets 171, INR 1.4, procalcitonin 4.8
- 16:30: T 101.4 F, HR 116, RR 26, MAP 67; piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g extended infusion started
- 16:45: vancomycin 1,750 mg load (20 mg/kg) started over 2 h
- 17:00: lactate 3.8; T 101.6 F, HR 122, RR 27, MAP 66; LR 500 mL bolus started
- 17:15: BP 101/44, MAP 63 despite bolus
- 17:30: norepinephrine started 0.05 mcg/kg/min via left IJ central line; MAP 64
- 17:45: second LR 500 mL bolus

**Current Status (about 17:50)**
HR 121, BP 102/45 (MAP 64) rising on norepinephrine 0.05, RR 27, SpO2 95% on FiO2 0.40, T 101.7 F. UOP 28 mL/h (15:00-16:00) then 24 mL/h (16:00-17:00), 0.3 mL/kg/h. RASS -2 on propofol 30, fentanyl 100; PIP up to 28 and Pplat 21 (from 24/17 this morning). SpO2 down from 98% at 14:00. Extremities warm, brisk cap refill, abdomen soft, bladder pressure last 12 mmHg at noon.

**Data**
Lactate 2.9 then 3.8. K 3.8, Mg 1.9, phosphorus 2.6 (after replacement), creatinine 1.1, glucose 226 (insulin infusion at 1.5 units/h). INR 1.4, aPTT 38, fibrinogen 380: no overt DIC, will trend. Hgb 11.6.

**Assessment**
Septic shock from burn wound infection (right chest/arm), with hypoperfusion (lactate 3.8, oliguria) and ongoing hypotension after 1 L crystalloid. SIRS criteria are unreliable in burn patients (baseline hypermetabolism, tachycardia, low-grade fever), but this trend is unmistakable: temperature above 101 F, HR above 120, RR above 26, new oliguria, rising lactate and falling MAP. Early hypoxemia and rising airway pressures suggest capillary leak/early ARDS physiology. Patient is already about 12% above Parkland, so further large boluses carry risk.

**Plan**
1. Hemodynamics: goal MAP 65 or higher. Titrate norepinephrine by 0.02-0.04 mcg/kg/min q5-10 min; vasopressin if above 0.25. Limit further crystalloid; albumin 5% 500 mL overnight. Repeat lactate at 19:00, goal clearance at least 10-20% q2h.
2. Antimicrobials: pip-tazo q8h and vancomycin per pharmacy AUC dosing. Cultures pending. Narrow at 48 h or with results.
3. Stress-dose hydrocortisone 50 mg IV q6h if norepinephrine requirement continues to rise.
4. Glucose: increase insulin infusion per protocol to goal 140-180.
5. Ventilator: at 18:00 raise PEEP to 8, FiO2 0.50, set RR 18 (total RR 27-28, early ARDS lung protection, keep VT 450, Pplat below 30). ABG 30-45 min after changes; portable CXR now. Increase sedation (propofol, fentanyl) for dyssynchrony.
6. Goals: MAP at least 65, UOP at least 0.5 mL/kg/h (41 mL/h), lactate downtrending, SpO2 92% or higher. Daily SAT deferred while in shock.
7. Continue heparin SQ prophylaxis (platelets monitored), pantoprazole.
8. Family (Jenna Whitaker, Linda Delaney) updated by Dr. Okafor. Full code.

Critical care time 55 minutes, excluding procedures.
L. Brandt, MD, Critical Care.

Wound infection recognized at 14:00; cultures x4 at 15:50; pip-tazo 16:30; vancomycin 1,750 mg load 16:45 (infusing until about 18:45); LR boluses x2; norepinephrine 17:30; mafenide soaks started 17:30; silver sulfadiazine discontinued. NKDA. Full Code.

**A**
- Vitals 18:30: T 102.1 F, HR 126, BP 108/48 (MAP 68), RR 29, SpO2 94%.
- Norepinephrine 0.10 mcg/kg/min (0.05 at 17:30, 0.08 at 18:00, 0.10 at 18:30), MAP goal 65 or higher.

- Lactate 3.8 (17:00). ABG 18:45: pH 7.31, PaCO2 36, PaO2 92, HCO3 18, BE -8, lactate pending.

- Lines: left IJ (norepinephrine, antibiotics on separate lumens), left radial A-line, left AC PIV, Foley, OG with feeds at 70 mL/h.

**R / To do**

notes.title: Portable Chest X-Ray, Single View
notes.author: Radiology Service, Diagnostic Radiology
notes.impression: Mild bilateral perihilar/interstitial opacities, no focal consolidation. ETT, OG tube and left IJ central line well positioned. Findings consistent with capillary leak / early ARDS physiology versus pulmonary edema.
notes.summary: Mild bilateral perihilar interstitial opacities without consolidation; support devices well positioned.
notes.body:
**Study**
Portable chest radiograph, single AP view, obtained 18:40.

**Clinical Indication**
Sepsis from burn wound infection, increasing oxygen requirement and airway pressures, ventilator changes (PEEP 8, FiO2 0.50).

**Comparison**
Chest radiograph 11/03/2026 05:00.

**Findings**
- Lines/tubes: Oral endotracheal tube tip approximately 4 cm above the carina. Orogastric tube with side port and tip below the diaphragm in the stomach. Left internal jugular central venous catheter tip at the cavo-atrial junction. ECG leads and monitoring wires overlie the chest.
- Lungs: New mild bilateral perihilar and interstitial opacities, symmetric, without dense focal consolidation or air bronchograms. No lobar collapse. Mild atelectasis at the right lung base unchanged.
- Pleura: No pneumothorax. No definite pleural effusion.
- Heart/mediastinum: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits for AP technique. No mediastinal widening.
- Bones/soft tissues: Right chest wall soft-tissue dressing material. No fracture or subcutaneous emphysema.

**Impression**
1. Mild bilateral perihilar/interstitial opacities, new since the prior study, no focal consolidation. Consistent with capillary leak / early ARDS physiology versus interstitial edema; clinical correlation advised.
2. ETT, OG tube and left IJ central line are well positioned.
3. No pneumothorax.

notes.title: Pharmacy Antimicrobial and Vancomycin Dosing Note
notes.author: A. Chen, PharmD
notes.summary: Vancomycin 1,750 mg load given, AUC-guided plan with level before second dose; pip-tazo extended infusion, compatibility and renal monitoring; supports hydrocortisone for pressor-dependent shock.
notes.body:
**Reason for Consult**
Antimicrobial dosing and monitoring, sepsis from early invasive right chest/arm burn wound infection (Dr. Okafor, Dr. Brandt). Weight 82 kg (dosing weight), height 180 cm, IBW 75 kg. No known drug allergies.

**Pertinent Data**
- Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL (17:00), estimated CrCl about 110 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, actual weight); BUN 27. Burn patients often have augmented clearance and a larger volume of distribution, but sepsis and hypoperfusion raise the risk of AKI (UOP 20-28 mL/h this evening).
- WBC 18.4, platelets 171, procalcitonin 4.8, lactate 3.8 (17:00), 4.1 (19:00).
- Cultures sent 15:50 before antibiotics: blood x2, wound, tracheal aspirate, urine.
- Vitals 19:30: T 102.4 F, HR 133, MAP 69 on norepinephrine 0.12 mcg/kg/min.

**Vancomycin**
- Loading dose 1,750 mg IV (20 mg/kg actual weight) given 16:45 over 2 hours.
- Plan: AUC/MIC-guided dosing (target AUC24 400-600) using Bayesian software. Anticipated maintenance 1,250 mg IV q12h, first dose due about 04:30, to be finalized from the level.
- Level: vancomycin level 15 minutes before the second dose (04:15) to estimate clearance; dose will be adjusted by pharmacy. No trough-only targeting.
- Renal monitoring: BMP q12h (creatinine today 1.1), strict UOP, avoid additional nephrotoxins (no NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides). Combination of vancomycin plus pip-tazo is associated with a higher risk of AKI; will watch closely and reassess need for vancomycin when cultures return. If MSSA is identified, will recommend switching to a beta-lactam.

**Piperacillin-Tazobactam**
4.5 g IV q8h as extended infusion over 4 hours (first dose 16:30). Rationale: time-above-MIC pharmacodynamics, augmented clearance and expanded volume of distribution in burn and septic patients, and need for reliable Pseudomonas and Gram-negative coverage. Next doses 00:30 and 08:30. No renal adjustment at this time.

**Compatibility and Administration**
- Vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam are Y-site incompatible at higher concentrations. Do not run through the same lumen simultaneously; flush with saline between agents. Suggest pip-tazo extended infusion via the left AC PIV or a dedicated lumen and vancomycin via a separate central lumen.
- Norepinephrine on a dedicated central lumen; propofol is lipid and should not be mixed with other drugs; insulin infusion on its own line.

**Other Review**
- VTE prophylaxis: heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h appropriate (platelets 171; if platelets fall below 100 or drop more than 50%, assess HIT).
- Stress ulcer prophylaxis: pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily appropriate (ventilated, burn greater than 20% TBSA, INR 1.4, steroids anticipated).
- Hydrocortisone: recommend stress-dose hydrocortisone 50 mg IV q6h if norepinephrine requirement continues at 0.1 mcg/kg/min or higher beyond about 1-2 hours (current 0.12). Monitor glucose (insulin infusion), potassium and sodium; plan taper once off vasopressors.
- Acetaminophen 1 g IV q8h scheduled: check LFTs daily (AST 72, ALT 58 this morning); max 3 g/day recommended.

A. Chen, PharmD, will follow cultures and levels.

notes.title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Assessment (Sepsis Peak)
notes.author: E. Haddad, RN

notes.body:

**Neuro**
